reviews.text: Highlight of our trip! We hiked Elephant Mountain 2 days prior, and this was so much better! Still a lot of stairs, but less popular and surrounded by gorgeous greenery. 10/10 recommend!

A Thread of Sky (一線天) is a striking natural feature located along the Xiangshan Trail, offering a unique and picturesque stop for hikers. This narrow rock formation creates a dramatic “slice” of sky between towering cliffs, making it a fascinating and photogenic spot that feels almost otherworldly.

Reaching A Thread of Sky involves a bit of climbing, but the trail leading there is manageable and well-marked. As you approach, the light filtering through the rocky crevice creates a stunning effect, especially during early morning or late afternoon. It’s a great place to pause, take in the beauty of nature, and capture some memorable photos.
Nice hiking trail, not crowded, well paved.
Natural formation of two rocks paving a way. worth the detour from the peak climb for a quick photo
This tiny walk through in between two giant stones is part of the lower route of Xiang Shan trail.

reviews.text: Jenny was amazing! We had a great tour! She taught us Taiwanese history and about the origins of foods, local culture and unique dishes to Taiwan. Several of the items that were on my list to try like stinky tofu and braised pork rice were included. If you’re at all on the fence - just go ahead and book it; you’ll have great food and meet some great people!

Our guide, Eddie, was incredible.  Outgoing, knowledgeable, kind, humorous…. Just the total package for my introduction to Taiwan food and culture.   The food was pretty good, but the company and guide was 5 star for sure!  Highly recommend!

I had a great time on the food tour! The people were very nice, including our guide Tâilé. She was also very knowledgeable, gave us a very good insight about the Taiwanese cuisine and, for example, gave us some tips about what drinks we could buy in the convenience store we went to. Highly recommended!

I’m not usually one for tours and like to point and try random things. I thought I would give this tour a go for something different.

Best decision I’ve made, largely thanks to the fun and info Roro the tour leader added! It was such a fun and informative tour, 10/10 recommend to anyone going to TPE.

Roro even took the time to give us all a lengthy list of other things to do in TPE and her favourite spots. If you can, ask for her as your guide!

Our guide Leo was very informative and shared lots of helpful information that made our food tour enjoyable. I have been to several night markets in the past, without any context and local knowledge. This tour gave us valuable food tour with information.
We plan to try several other tour programs to enrich our experience.

reviews.text: Visited here to celebrate valentines day. Suitable for couple or family with kids for a romantic getaway! With different zone to explore and have some nice lavender ice cream or lavender latte! The staff 澄钰 very friendly and recommended us some tips! Awesome!

Very expensive for entry and they give you 100nt tokens to take off when you buy in the grounds, but it’s very expensive, for example a coffee is 180nt for just a basic black coffee.

The ice cream they sell is 150nt with token you still need to pay 50nt. If you’re giving token I think items should be a small bit lower in cost, everything is inflated.

The one star is solely because of the cost it’s very expensive considering the local cost in Taiwan.

The ground are beautiful and well kept, staff are nice, the girl at the entry where you buy the ticket is really nice.

I don’t think I’d comeback due to the cost. But overall was a nice experience.

Unless you drive , otherwise, it’s a long way to visit there. And, It’s relatively small that I expected.

Maybe I visited it in late September and low season, not many places are truly spectacular compared to the lavender season.

And you have to be creative if you want to take some great photos with different flowerings season.

Lavender are not in full bloom until Jan - Feb of the year, so be prepared for very sparse lavenders. The place is well organised, and for the tickets you paid, there will be tokens worth 100TWD to encourage spending within the premises.

Is a great cosy place to visit. It's my second time visiting this place but you need to book a car because it's in a forest, no public transport. They had expanded more space for people to visit. Is all surrounded with trees and nature, so there will be some mosquito and bugs, so I need to spray mosquito repellent before going in.
Time i went, the Lavender just grew back, and it's in a different colour. Looks really pretty.

reviews.text: It looks beautiful from outside but I am really not sure what to see inside. I spent about 10 minutes at the museum, mostly browsing through the souvenir counter. Maybe you should come to check in because Taichung is famous for its sun cakes, and it’s free of charge. Plus, it’s right in the downtown area and close to the train station.

The DIY Sun Cake Workshop is a must-try if you visit Taichung! The instructor was friendly and very knowledgeable on the history and process of making Sun Cakes. Each person will get to make 6 Sun Cakes and it comes it a cute box!

You can sign up through their website but it is in Chinese, so you will need to translate. There is a maximum as well as minimum pax for each lesson, so book early (1-2 weeks before) but be prepared for timeslot changes if your selected timeslot has too few participants. The lesson itself is also in Chinese so it would be useful to have someone who understands Chinese join in... otherwise you can just follow the motion... haha

The museum itself is just some panels of information so it's not that interesting. The highlight is really the DIY workshop.

We signed up for a DIY sun cake class at the museum. The instructor had decades of sun cake baking experience. Very patient and interactive. He was passionate about his craft and an ambassador of promoting this treasured Taichung delicacy. The sun cake was DELICIOUS 😋  Communication with the staff was top-notched. Everyone was welcoming and made our visit to the museum the most enjoyable. Upstairs is the museum that not only explains the history of sun cake, but also the architecture of the building and the surrounding neighborhood. Also have an art show of drawings and paintings.
We highly recommend this museum and especially the DIY class. One of the most fun things we've done in Taichung so far.
The sun cake class is amazing! You can make your own sun cake in 90 mins. The teacher is a very benign uncle. You need to book in advance. good experience!

While its name is a museum, it is really a gift shop with a workshop where people can learn how to make sun cakes.   The upper level does a basic job of explaining the process of sun cake making.   Overall, it's really a gift shop but the sun cake is really good.

reviews.text:
Spacious room with wide windows. There are no taller buildings in the view so you can get a clear view of the sky!

Room and toilet is clean. Plenty of plugs to use.

Service is great. We tried room service and the portion of the food is quite big.

It’s connected to Far Eastern mall which is convenient.

Wasn’t able to use the gym but we checked them out and they have plenty of equipment (ex: has squat racks).

I only had breakfast several days in a row since the buffet is more plentiful. The overall impression of the hotel is, as largely reviewed, a bit aged. It often takes a long time until one of the elevators arrive on ground level or on room level, also during off-peak times. Often the number of people waiting is getting large. It is recommended to leave the room five minutes earlier if you have appointments. Otherwise I like the hotel. The building is also quite photogenic from several perspectives as my attached photos might show.

We recently stayed in an executive floor suite at Shangri-La Far Eastern, Tainan for three nights and were thoroughly impressed with the service. The staff’s attentiveness and proactive approach, especially Shiuan and Lana’s meticulous care in the Lounge, made our stay a truly memorable one. Compared to other hotels we’ve stayed at in Taiwan, this experience not only met but exceeded our expectations. The level of service and attention to detail truly set Shangri-La Far Eastern, Tainan apart, delivering an impressive service that makes it a stay worth recommending.

Great place to stay, international Breakfast with a big choice. Can be a bit noisy when fully booked and traffic jams at the elevator may occur in morning rush hour.

reviews.text:
The rooms in this still relatively new hotel are clean and minimalistic with wooden flooring. The service was good, and the staff was attentive.
I did not like the breakfast at all. Choices are limited, and the omelet I ordered had almost cold ingredients despite the outside temperature.
For breakfast, I chose a daily 20 min walk to the near by Shangri-la, where the breakfast choices are plentiful, though the rooms are understood to be stuffy and old.

Grand Banyan is a fairly new hotel with minimalistic vibes. The gym is on the smaller end but everything feels clean. They also offer free wash/dry, but you’ll have to pay 20NT for pods if you don’t have detergent.

They also don’t provide toiletries in accordance with the upcoming restrictions - but they do provide standard shampoo and body gel only.

I thought it was fine that the toilet was separate from the main bathroom, but found it weird there was no soap readily available. That was a bit off-putting.

Excellent hotel staff who are very helpful. Conceige was nice to help reserve restaurant and make recommendation. Reception is really professional too. room is spacious and comfy, and conveniently located ( about 20 minutes walk to many sightseeing) . Highly recommended.
Located near the Tainan Train Station, it is easily accessible.  The room is quiet, clean and spacious.  The staff are friendly and helpful.  Everything is great and I like this hotel so much.

Clean. Big rooms. Nice showers. But limited amenities: no water bottles, lotion, toilettes, etc. encountered some issues like noise and lights blowing out. Other that than, good option for a nice hotel in Tainan.

reviews.text:
We have been like a regular customer and have stayed at this hotel a lot of times with my family already in the past this place was very very good.
The food,the service,the cleanliness,but…it fell off hard. Recently when I visited this hotel I found out that the breakfast standards dropped so much,it was still edible but…it wasn’t as good u know? I’m also about to say something that might make you guys freak out and not want to stay here, there was a glass shard on the floor. It wasn’t big but I stepped on it and my leg hurt,maybe the staff didn’t vacuum the floor thoroughly but I’m just saying that a child might get hurt, so…and room even didn’t provide toilet paper roll. Anyways ,the whole room is a square bro,other hotel are like rectangle and shit but this room is a square which make it so claustrophobic! Anyway on to the good part, The hair dryer was so nice! It wasn’t very hot like your scalp was burning when you used it. And as you might know,there are earthquakes and so electricity might be cut off and they provided a literal torchlight!
First time! Like they all say safety first am I right? Another thing is that the lobby has a little book to write or draw some stuff to show that you have visited and stayed in that hotel which is so cute. Overall ,this place is quite ok.
An amazing hotel experience. Rooms are on the smaller side but very well appointed and spotlessly clean. The service was stellar. The breakfast buffet was very good value.

Pleasant stay.  Room was spacious and room layout is practical.  Seperate shower to toilet and wash basin also seperate.  Makes sharing a room easy.  Water pressure in shower was good.  Hotel was modern and clean.

Room had free snacks and also free bottled water which can get replenished.  Had mini fridge and hairdryer.  Also provided slippers.

Free breakfast was nice.  Not a lot of variety (or changes) however sufficient for a short stay.

Only one lift so can be slow especially since hotel had 10 levels.

Room had aircond which was refreshing in the heat but can be a bit cold at night.  Mattress was firm and light switches were plenty however can be a bit confusing which controlled which.

Tainan station is walkable however beware that if you have luggage, it’s a bit of a pain as the pathways were not designed for pedestrians.  So you are practically sharing the road with cars which can be a bit overwhelming.  We ended up taking a taxi to hotel which costs NTD85, felt much safer that way.

Two convenience stores within walking distance.

Would recommend

A very cozy hotel located in an excellent location. The breakfast they provided was excellent and very worth it. Our rooms were super clean and the shower was spacious. We also especially liked the provided shampoo and body wash, they had a really nice scent.

The staff went above and beyond to accommodate us during typhoon Gaemi. We were in Hualien the day before, and because of the typhoon we were unable to commute to the hotel on that day. The hotel staff allowed us to change our dates of stay last minute free of charge and we are extremely thankful for that.

Check in and out usually take awhile when there are a lot of guests at the same time, recep staffs able to manage and handle it fast . They able to answer your enquiries mannerly. Staffs went for extra miles to check on my enquiry of housekeeping and call for cab when I was anxious of running late to train station. Thankful for the recep ladies!!

Check-in and check-out can take some time when there’s a crowd, but the reception staff manage it efficiently. They also respond to inquiries politely. I’m especially grateful to the reception team for going the extra mile to check on my housekeeping request and arrange a cab when I was worried about being late for the train. Big thanks to the reception ladies!

The overall environment could use some improvement, especially in cleanliness, as I noticed dust near the window. I stayed in a Superior Room with a window on a high floor, near the lift. The sound insulation was average, but I think that’s more due to guests' behavior. I did enjoy the high floor and the nice view, though I heard some sounds near the curtain at night, possibly birds outside.

Breakfast was decent, and the location is great—close to a bus stop, retail stores, including food and sportswear shops, and bubble tea spots!

reviews.text: Everything was excellent! The room was great, the amenities were top-notch, and the breakfast was fantastic ( Chinese food 2nd floor). Here are 2 restaurants that you can choose for breakfast. The staff was incredibly accommodating, fulfilling every request. Thank you, Silk Place Tainan! If I visit Tainan again, I’ll definitely stay here. Ps.The bed is a bit hard but acceptable.

Best hotel to stay. Excellent location with everything nearby. The rooms are spacious, clean and comfortable. Suggest to stay in the executive floor where you can taste sumptuous breakfast with drinks through the day. Staff is friendly. What's more, the restaurants are must try. We had the seasonal menu in Robin's with the famous Rouge Duck   The outdoor swimming pool with a bar serving creative tea cocktails and live music is sensational

This is a 5 star hotel but the room does not reflect the 5-star quality and value. I’ve booked the junior suite king room for its spaciousness and big tub. The room looks exactly like the pictures, but we quickly noticed the room smells like the combination of old sewer and street food. We asked the hotel to provide some air refreshers, which the staffs very helpfully provided an air purifier. Unfortunately it didn’t help. We suspect the smell came from the centralized AC vent.

The bedroom while large needs a refresh and the shower head adjustment need’s adjusting.
You have to book to buy a beer in the 4f bar so we went elsewhere. The breakfast is fine but the room is too busy.

Really convenient location in the middle of Tainan with good facilities available - gym and swimming pool.

The room was also very spacious and clean! I love the tub as well, allowing me to unwind after a long day. The only downside was that the pillows were not very good and sink very easily. I had a bad back for the entire day after waking up.

Service was really good as well and the lobby staff were all very friendly! Hope they improve their pillows but otherwise, a good stay!

reviews.text: Clean and simple, nothing fancy here. But, it's a 2 minute walk to the Taipei Main Station, so super-convenient for tourists wishing to travel around the city and indeed the country!

Location is great.  Just a few metres away from M8 access to Taipei Main Station. Easy to find food. Room is dated but alright.  No kettle in room but provided hot cold water dispenser near lift.  Our room has no view, only window looking out to air well. Bed is harder than my liking. Staff friendly and helpful.

The room is nice and the location is very accessible with 7-11 and Familymart nearby. There is also a 新光 nearby as well as various shops and of course Taipei main station which has HSR HRA and the Metro. There is an entrance to the station one block away. There is barely any amenities inside the hotel besides laundry 40nt for wash 20nt for dry but it barely dries. You can place your luggage in early before your check in time. Comes with 2 towels soap toothbrush comb shampoo body wash razor .

Very nice hotel near Taipei Main Station. Strategic location, 3min walk from M8 exit (with escalator) from Taipei Metro station.
Deluxe room is well equipped, with comfortable bed and electronic bidet toilet seat!
Normal twin bed room is less nice, the renovation is simple as compare to deluxe one.
Forgot to take my phone after checkout. Contacted them via email and they replied within short period of time. Yup, found back my phone as well.
Highly recommended this hotel.

I feel there is no hospitality among the staff. (Maybe it depends on the person.) I asked the front desk staff to arrange a taxi to the airport the next morning, but they refused, saying that you have to make the call. This is the only hotel in Taipei that refused to arrange a taxi. Also, I contacted them in advance in English, either by email or via the booking website, with an enquiry or request, I could not get a reply at all.

reviews.text:
Cosmo Hotel is conveniently located near Taipei Main Station (50 metres to nearest M3 entrance/exit) making it a great choice for easy access to transportation and exploring the city.

Pros:
•	Service: The hotel provides excellent service, with attentive staff.
•	Location: Its proximity to Taipei Main Station is a major plus for travelers.
•	Room Size: The family room is spacious, offering ample space for guests to move around comfortably.

Cons:
•	Double Bed Size and toilet : While the rooms are spacious, the double bed may feel smaller than expected. The showing area is quite tight too.

•	Noise: The soundproofing could be better; you might hear noise from neighboring rooms or the floor above, such as conversations or children playing (depending on your neighbours)

Overall, Cosmo Hotel offers a great stay in terms of location and service.

The hotel is conveniently located just beside Taipei train station, making it easier to travel outside Taipei. Plenty of eateries n retail shops nearby. The staff team is also super friendly and accommodating. They also allocated my parents an elderly friendly room which is really thoughtful.

I represent a group of 50+ people, some with special needs, staying at Cosmos Hotel Taipei from 1 Dec to 4 Dec.

Claire, the Sales Manager, has been extremey patient with our communications, catering to the needs of our special needs from the start.

Shane, the Front Desk Officer, shown great empathy and understanding towards our group the moment we arrived and until we left.

We weren't only impressed by their service standard, the families enjoyed the variety offered at the buffet breakfast too!

And of course, the convenience of the hotel is excellent - right by the Main Station exit, and it leads to various places via the underground walkways / malls.

The group is truly appreciative and grateful for what they have done / offered our group to make our already amazing trip even better!

The wall partition is very thin. You can hear noise from Next Door, including day and night noise. The air conditioner only has a fan speed adjustment, but can not adjust temperature. If you feel cold and turn off the fan, then you will get the smell coming out from the toilet.

Very helpful and warm front desk staff. Very good location because it is right by all the stations - HSR, metro etc . They even give us welcome drink voucher at the cafe. It is a true value-for-money hotel.

reviews.text:
Nice hotel in great location. Minutes from MRT station and there was bus stop just across the road. We had requested a quiet room and they provided just that. Staffs are very attentive and helpful to the best of their ability.

Also loving the washing-drying facilities they have. Very reasonable price and it's so good to have fresh clean clothes done inside the hotel instead of having to walk around looking for a coin laundry. Hopefully they will have more washer/dryer machine as the machines (2 pairs) are always in use!

It's not near a MRT station, but there is a bus stop in front of the hotel. The rooms are clean and somewhat new, however they are similar to the compacted Japanese hotel rooms. The breakfasts tasty decent, but options are somewhat limited and they serve the same food everyday. There is no gym in the building. At their price point, I will likely find a different hotel that is closer to the MRT the next time I visit.

This review is based on the value of the property for the price we paid (~$3600NTD/night on avg)

Firstly, we booked an accessibility/king bed room in the 11th floor. The room was very small, basically the door opens and the bed is right in front, but it was liveable. The room included a humble sized closet, mini fridge, small desk, and tv. The washroom, however, was about the same size as the room itself. We had two strollers that took up the entire "empty" space that was available between the entryway and desk. In sum, a small room but it worked.

The washroom is the no divider style, unless you use the bathtub which we did not want to use. The sink does not come with a vanity, so it was just a sink and no countertop space for anything else. Less functional, but still we made it work. Toilet, sink, and shower all worked just fine. However, the ventilation is extremely poor. Basically everything we hung in the washroom dried poorly.

The bed was comfortable, HOWEVER, I do suspect "uncleanliness" (dust? Others?) because we (2 adults+2 toddlers) all had a couple/few very small red bumps that don't look or itch the same way as mosquito bites. This is my biggest concern and reflected in my rating.

Otherwise, we thoroughly enjoyed the complimentary breakfast over our 15 night stay. Food was fresh and tasty. Although, on the last few days the daily veggies went from cabbage to bean sprouts. The kitchen staff was friendly, hardworking, and there to deliver a great service every single day. We miss them!

The only thing I did voice directly to staff is concern about the safety of the accessibility ramp to the lobby. It is located off to the side of the staircased main entrance. Most nights, the light for this ramp entrance was off. It was dark until you fully stepped into the lobby. Occasionally, the light was on. We pushed strollers with toddlers and never felt unsafe, mostly because my husband was always around. However the experience could be very different for others.

Staff said the light is controlled by the restaurant, so it depends on the restaurant and they - the hotel - have no control. This was an unacceptable answer to me. The accessibility ramp is part of the hotel entrance, then the light should be part of the hotel's accessibility and safety considerations, not left to the restaurant. I hope management can take this into serious reconsideration; it should not be a complicated issue to resolve.

Overall, would recommend:)

it seems cheaper if you book direct from hotel website.
bed is comfortable, bathtub is huge and fill up so fast, standing shower pressure is good, room is spacious (i book their smallest room).
breakfast taste average, but i like the fact that they change almost all the dishes during our 3 days there.
location is good also, need to walk about 8mins from the mrt station on flat ground so drag luggage is fine.
there is direct bus to keelung, and many other popular places.
pretty value for money, recommended!

I had a fantastic stay at the Green World Hotel Grand Nanjing. The rooms are impressively spacious and immaculately clean, providing a very comfortable experience. The bathrooms are a standout feature, offering both a large bathtub and a separate shower, along with a modern Japanese toilet. If you appreciate well-designed, spacious accommodations, this hotel is an excellent choice!

Pros:
-room is spacious and has all the basic amenities
-bed and pillows are super comfortable
-cleaning staff did a great job keeping the room tidy and clean
-receptionists are polite and efficient
-price is reasonable for the room

Cons:
-although the hotel is next to the metro, the location itself feels very isolated and there’s pretty much nothing to do in the area, the area is not very walkable either with tons of traffic on busy and narrow streets and ongoing construction. Overall it feels like a somewhat rundown area. In addition, although the metro station is nearby, you’ll likely take at least two lines (i.e a transfer) if you want to go to any popular tourist spot
-the gym does not belong to the hotel, it’s 3 minutes walk from the hotel but the gym feels very crowded as the gym seems to have agreements with several nearby hotels while also running as an independent commercial gym so it’s quite busy

Overall, good hotel for a budget stay, the major downside is location. That said, taxis in Taiwan are pretty cheap so if you don’t mind spending time commuting to downtown area, it’s a good stay.

Great hotel with great service! The beds are really comfortable, there are nice places to sit outside and inside, and a good breakfast (possibility to choose between three options). We could leave our luggage in the hotel the day we checked out (which is also already later than most hotels, at 12 PM), and they gave us free noodles for the night the typhoon was there 🙏🏻
Good clean rooms. Nice staffs. Free coffee and tea from morning to afternoon. Convenient location to St Ignatius MRT station.

There are many things to love about this hotel. The negative is it requires a 40 min train ride from the city but the metro is easy, safe and efficient. As a bonus, there’s a direct bus to the National Palace which is 40 mins away (bus 815).

Here’s two things we loved.

1. The hotel gives you free access to the gym across the road and it’s excellent - far bigger and better than an ordinary hotel gym.

2. The rooms are spacious for Taiwan and extremely well designed to make life comfortable and easy. And you can open the door to the balcony for fresh air.

From the moment we required assistance, your team went above and beyond to ensure we were well cared for. Their promptness in arranging a cab for us to visit the doctor was greatly appreciated, as were the thoughtful gestures such as offering water, tissues, and plastic bags while we waited. Thank you for these small but meaningful acts of kindness

When we needed to extend our stay at the last minute, the staff’s efforts to accommodate us despite the hotel being fully booked were extraordinary. They graciously offered us the last available room, a special-access room, at a special rate. This level of flexibility and empathy exemplifies the high standards of hospitality.

I'm impressed with the consistent and genuine concern shown by your team throughout our stay. Each time we interacted with staff—be it at breakfast, the front desk, or during check-out—they expressed heartfelt concern for my son’s well-being. Their kind words and cheerful demeanor brightened his spirits.

Please extend our sincere thanks to every member of your team who contributed to making our stay as comfortable as possible. Their dedication and care left a lasting impression on us, and we will remember this experience with great appreciation.

reviews.text: The location of this place is excellent. It manages to maintain a quiet atmosphere despite being in a busy area. It's not far from the Civic Square and the adjacent pedestrian street, yet the rooms are very quiet. The room isn't large, but I really like the hair dryer here. Usually, the hair dryers in hotels don't have much power, but this one is great. There is a small issue though. There's always a smell of paint wafting into my room. I'm not sure if it's from a new installation or fresh paint somewhere. If you're traveling with kids, it might be a good idea to check with the front desk. Since I'm only staying for two days, I didn't dwell on it too much and didn't ask to change rooms. That's about it. Looking forward to the next time.

The hotel is situated in a part of the city which is choc-a-bloc with both shopping and eating outlets. It is also
across from a pedestrianised area which turned into a vibrant area on Friday as families and young couples came out to take part in  the Christmas festivities.
The rooms are nice but have some quirks such as no drinking water in the room but has to be fetched from a water cooler. There was teaching and coffee but no milk and sugar, and no spoons to stir either. The bathrooms have some basic amenities like shampoo and a basic toiletries kit but spending from 2025, those have to be purchased as new government regulations on conservation kick in.
The breakfast was really good, especially the variety of dumplings on offer for breakfast.
Staying there due to a 2-night business trip. The room really shows the history, but still comfy enough. It is quite nice that some floors have free sparkling water dispensers.
Room is clean. Service is excellent. (The person at the door could called the cab for you.) Central to every place that's interesting. I will definitely coming back.
Amenities not good. Dated and dirty. Hotel staff not welcoming. Convenient location and breakfast is pretty good.

reviews.text: Rooms were clean, good bathroom and shower and everything was fulfilling, abit compact. Definitely not luxury, but in the center of city, provided all necessities. Very child-friendly, has a floor for children to play. No parking outside, outside of hotel is cluttered, no walkable footpath with motorcycles that don’t stop at anything. nice buffet with a wide range of foods, no bacon or some other western foods though. Had high quality gelato and sorbet. Has a stop for food delivery. Room service is normal.

The room that cost more than NTD$7,000  a night has no windows and no washlet made me a bit stunned. The mattress was very hard, the pillows were not good to sleep on, and the sound insulation was not very good.There's a big TV in the room which is nice but the multimedia system could be richer!
The  playground on the 9th floor is spacious and well designed for little children.
Brunch is extraordinary with high CP value!

Phoenix Hotel made out stay in Taichung a pleasant one!

The staff were friendly and helpful. We needed to buy an essential item online (for our two year old daughter) using a Taiwanese shopping app but it was not available for us to download, so we asked if the staff could do us a favour and purchase it for us. They helped to ask the seller if there was stock and if it could be delivered asap. Unfortunately due to typhoon it would not be delivered to us in time. Nevertheless, we were grateful for their willingness to help us. They continued to search online to see if we could purchase the item at any nearby department stores.

The room we booked was clean and spacious for two adults and a toddler. We were able to fit a portacot in the room for our daughter.

Our daughter loved playing in the hotels playroom! There were a variety of activities for children - dress ups and role playing, car racing, slides and climbing equipment, and a couple of arcade games. The play areas were large and spacious.

We also enjoyed the buffet breakfast every morning! There was so much food to choose from and it was all very delicious. From a variety of breads and spreads, cereals, salads, cold drinks, tea, coffee, dim Sims, Korean food, Taiwanese food, Chinese food, Japanese food, western food, and even haagen dazs icecream!

Location-wise, I think we were further away from Taichung's CBD but riding an uber to get around was very convenient.

Overall, a great hotel :)
Came with family and stayed one night. Room was very small and minimally stocked with no slippers provided. Luckily breakfast was good with wide spread .

The room was spacious, clean, and well-maintained, providing a very comfortable stay. I also loved the beautiful decorative architecture, which added a unique charm to the hotel. Highly recommend!

We spent our New Year’s Eve 2025 at Han Hsien Hotel in Kaohsiung, and it was an unforgettable experience. While the hotel is situated a bit farther from the nearest station, making transportation slightly less convenient, the quality of our stay more than made up for it.

Upon arrival, there was a delay in the check-in process, which initially left us a bit disappointed. However, the hotel staff quickly turned things around by providing us with a high-quality room that offered a stunning view of the city. Watching the New Year’s Eve fireworks from the comfort of our room was truly magical.

The hotel also went the extra mile by including additional freebies, which was a pleasant surprise. To top it off, we enjoyed a complimentary breakfast buffet, which featured a variety of delicious options to start our new year on a delightful note.

Overall, despite a few minor inconveniences, Han Hsien Hotel delivered a wonderful experience with its exceptional room quality and thoughtful service. It’s a great choice for anyone looking to celebrate special occasions in Kaohsiung!

The indoor pool and gym are actually quite good except they don't open until 9am and are not accessible by elevator.   My wife has knee problems and couldn't use these facilities because more than a full flight of stairs is required to get to 8th floor.  Overall I do not recommend this hotel.

We were pleasantly surprised that the hotel offers breakfast and even light snacks from 3pm to 10pm daily. Coffee machine is also available in the lobby and room amenities can be self-helped in the lobby as well. Washing powder is available complimentary when you do your laundry in the basement. It's these little perks that makes our stay at River Inn exceptional - did i mention that they even provide a shiatsu massager in the room? On top of that, our room was sufficiently spacious for 2 person and every corner was perfectly clean. Every design was also well thought after. There was a day where we dropped by for breakfast late and they were about the clear the dishes. However, they informed us on that and made sure we had sufficient time to grab our food before they cleared the buffet line. They even check with us again if we needed any more coffee before they proceeded to clean the machine. Every crew on the team was conscientious and we were so impressed at their hospitable service and thoughtfulness. We had such a comfortable and delightful stay. reviews.text:
I’m guessing this hotel has seen far better days. Both receptionists we encountered were rude and impatient. I was taken aback to witness someone treat my mother with such disrespect, especially because Taiwanese hospitality is legendary, and culturally, Taiwanese are respectful toward elders.  It really felt as though we were imposing on them during check-in (came early to drop off luggage).

I suppose I can deal with snooty staff, maybe chalk it up to a stressful week for them both, but the rooms were mediocre and dingy too. The toilet wouldn’t stop running unless the handle was jiggled in just the right way. I had been looking forward to using the jacuzzi/bath, but it’s evident the tub hasn’t been properly cleaned in some time.   The hotel is in great need of a refresh/new management. How on earth are the ratings even this high?

**edit: I’m raising the rating to 3 stars because the manager tracked down my mom and apologized profusely to her. I think there is clear room for improvement, but I appreciate the manager’s willingness to try and make amends.**

Medium-sized hotel for business and tourists. Interior feels rather modern and quite well kept. Location is about 10~15 walk from the nearest metro stations, but the hotel does have a parking lot, so driving here is no problem. Breakfast  contains small selection of of continental and Chinese dishes, and surprisingly can be rather filling. Service here is friendly and attentive, and I believe English is ok.

The location is convenient. MRT station pretty nearby... within walking distance. The service staff were very friendly and helpful to provide all the necessary information.

The only thing about it is that - the managing 'style' is very 'old school'... You need to drop your room key at the reception everytime you go out... No sneaking out... LOL Because they will 'catch' at the reception before you step out and ask you for the key. LOL

The room was huge and spacious. Though it said it's a non-smoking room, I can still smell the lingering of tobacco... That's not very nice.

Price is okay for the last minute selection.
But the room has a bit of smell and the decor is super outdated and the furnitures are worn

Comes with mosquitoes when you open the door.
Bathtub like cleaned last week or so.

But staff were friendly and nice. But probably won’t come back for that.

Its wallet friendly, staff is super helpful and kind and try to assist you the best way they can. Room are spacious and comfy. And breakfast is really good and buffet style. Definetly reccomend , specially for the budget.

The 5* reviews are fake. They all have the same generic messages and get posted at the same time.
The food was dry and bland and the restaurant was completely empty. Ruined a lovely day in Tainan.
We were recommended this "caviar" which is one of the most inedible things I've ever been served at a restaurant.

With a tour group. Walking in from the main door, you will be treated with a grand entrance of the oriental dinning hall view. So the more popular dishes are generally served to the tourists. Had their signature Egg Noodle (蛋蛋面). Silky egg noodle with Clear soup. For a Singaporean like me, Fish porridge is good. 清淡。meat balls are tasty. First serving is the cold dish. A very local dining restaurant. The egg noodle is a must try. I believe they should have very good dishes for dinner. Yes, highly recommended. 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻
Pretty good food. The restaurant is absolutely beautiful. The decor is awe-inspiring with tall ceilings and intricately carved light fixtures and wood trim. Truly stunning.

Highly recommended if you want to try out all the traditional Tainan deli in one place.
Fresh ingredients and friendly service.

The food tastes much more better than I thought, do try out the Dan Zai Noodle, tofu pudding, as well as the set menu here ( best for group of 2-3 people )

Expect some of the local dishes does not match your taste bud, for example the thick soup is too sweet for me, but overall I think it’s a pleasant dining experience.

Would definitely come back for more :)

Only went here because of the high rating on google but it turns out those glowing reviews are clearly made by a bot after closer inspection. The food was really quite bad and the place is nothing more than a tourist trap designed to empty your wallet and ruin your appetite. And we followed the waiters’ recommendations, so you can’t even say we ordered badly! Save yourself the disappointment and steer clear. One star (which I very rarely leave).

reviews.text:
A friend recommended this well known traditional Taiwanese restaurant.

Food: 4/5 - we enjoyed the steamed fresh prawns and chicken herbal soup. I was disappointed with the steamed mud crab with sticky rice. The crab was small and didn’t have much meat for that particular crab. The herbal soup was flavorful and tasty. Something my mom used to make.

Service: 3/5 - lots of servers standing around but not as attentive. We had a bottle of sake & ended up serving ourselves.

Atmosphere: 4/5 - bright and clean inside. They had fresh Easter lilies in vases. If you don’t like the scent as is, it may affect your meal.

This place is very famous for their crab with sticky rice but I am very disappointed. We ordered takeout because we don’t have reservation and it’s possible we had different quality of food. we waited for about 15 minutes for our food, in my experience it takes more than 15 minutes to cook the rice. I am fairly certain the rice is precooked separately not together with the crab.
And the rice is soggy, it does not have the right chew you expect from sticky rice. The quality of this dish definitely does not match the hype and the price they charge. Not recommended!!

This is a very famous restaurant in Tainan city where you can get the traditional banquet dishes in the old times.
The price is reasonable, dishes are yummy, service is quite prompt.
We ordered almost all the signature dishes, in the end, the restaurant offers free dishes of fruit and desserts, very sweet.

The stars are given based on this single trip.
The service was pretty good for sure. I didn’t make an early reservation, but they managed to squeeze a table for me. I really appreciated them.
The dishes were awesome even though I didn’t get to try their signature. The only thing I can be picky about is the soup. It was too sweet. Oh, and it would be nice if the yummy fried rice was a bit more.

Very well known for traditional Taiwanese cuisine.  The restaurant itself is a piece of history.

Food is quite good with the set menu catered to smaller groups of people who also wish to try most of their famous dishes. However, I would still suggest go with a big group of people and order their signature dishes in big servings to get the maximum traditional Taiwanese banquet experience.

A very good place to introduce Taiwanese cooking/culture to foreigners

reviews.text: The restaurant is spacious and cozy. The owner is very enthusiastic and kind. There is usually very crowded but the food is served very quickly. Fresh local food and fill your hunger pangs. The location is easy to find and has convenient parking. Highly recommended.

Our friends took us to this local beef hotpot restaurant for dinner, it’s quite a unique dining experience. Food was good and the beers and wines are very reasonably priced, selection was also better than expected. However, we saw a few big “insects” that really bothered us.

It’s famous for the hand sliced local beef, which is fresh and not been frozen. The hotpot had lots of miscellaneous ingredients inside, and lots more you can order more from the menu. And there are lots of sauces, ginger slices and vinegar you can mix for your own taste, I like the spicy fermented bean paste, while there are other simple choices like soy sauce or you can also eat it without.

Atmosphere is good and a wide variety of food to choose from. Hotpot is the popular selection, can order some local dishes as well. Call to reserve table in advance as there is always a waiting queue.
Very recommended dining place in Tainan!!

I visited this restaurant every time I came to Tainan. Comfortable seats. Air-conditioned. Delicious fresh beef hotpot. Pork (梅肉) and squid meatballs are also recommended. The aged steak is surprisingly good with the hotpot. The cold-brewed tea is a good pairing with the food. Crafted beer is available as well. A restaurant suitable for family and friend gatherings. Price is reasonable.

This is one of the more famous hot pot places in Tainan, and it didn't disappoint. The soup is amazing! We also ordered the giant grilled prawns which were cooked perfectly. They bottle their own tea, we got two different bottles and I think they were quite good. Good place for group. The staffs were extremely friendly and accommodating as we had two young kids with us.

reviews.text: This is a gorgeous restaurant with amazing food and impressive service. We tried the Surf and Turf and it was delicious. The lobster 🦞 was tender, succulent and full of taste. The Ribeye steak 🥩 was excellent. French 🇫🇷 onion soup was piping hot and authentic. Parma Ham and melon also perfect. Overall it was a great dining experience. I recommend you try this restaurant if you visit Tainan.  The prices are on the high side for Taiwan 🇹🇼

I love everything, especially the steak. It was perfectly cooked for my liking. The saltiness was also just right for me. Though they provide salt and sauces if one prefers a saltier or a more complex taste. The salad was refreshingly good for my palate and the dessert at the end tasted delicious as well. It was sweet with a mix of bitterness from the caramel. Totally worth the price. I was so full at the end.

All our steaks were cooked perfectly medium rare. The grilled pork chops were amazing, it was one of the best things I ate on that trip. My sister loved the lamb chops with mint sauce.  Overall the food was excellent! Looking forward to eating here again when we visit Tainan.

The Corner Steak House in Tainan offers a great dining experience with a unique Italian style ambiance. The restaurant is quite spacious, which is perfect for accommodating large groups of people.

One of the standout features of the restaurant is its excellent service. The staff is attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable, making for a truly enjoyable dining experience.

In terms of the food, the menu offers a variety of options, including a winery section with a range of options to choose from. The prices are also reasonable, making it a great value for the quality of food and service provided.

Overall, if you're looking for a romantic dinner or a special date night, the Corner Steak House in Tainan is definitely worth checking out. Be sure to make a reservation in advance, as it's a popular spot and tends to fill up quickly.

It is a quite small restaurant with only a few tables and everyone is seated and served at the same time so meals can take a while (3-4 hours). Food is delicious and the wines are pairings are nicely matched with the different courses. Will definitely be back next time I am in Tainan!

From the dining environment to the creative dishes, I had had a fantastic night at Principe!
The chef pays tribute to his root by reimagining the traditional Taiwanese cuisine with French cooking. For example, the Fricassée de poulet with French toast resembles the “coffin bread”, one of the best known street food in Tainan. Other dishes including, milkfish pie, oyster consommé and shrimp chips, also exhibit the flavours of An-Ping Old Street and An-Ping Port.
There are much more surprises that you have to experience yourself. Highly recommend ❤️

I write this as a cousin of the owner of the restaurant, Cheng Yu. Although it's easy to be biased due to the familial relations, I write this with the utmost sincerity.
I really looked forward to dining here even before they opened as Cheng Yu had shared with me that this has been a childhood dream of his and we had the opportunity to dine here as a private function with family members. Wait staff was extremely attentive, very professional in her explanations on each course and accommodating towards our needs.
I ordered the Fish whereas my husband had the Pork. The dishes were beautifully presented and tasted equally as enticing as it looked. The mushrooms on the side of the Pork was buttery and seasoned well with the Yuzu Sauce a delight to match with the Pork! Beautiful explosion of flavours!
I don't normally go for a Fish dish but I had a feeling that Principe would do an outstanding job and I wasn't wrong. The Swallowtail Fish was soft and had a lovely slightly crunchy skin and when paired with the foam, it was simply a great match. I would gladly eat this again.

Each dish was beautifully presented and the quality of the food was delicious.
It's quite obvious to me that each course had been well-contemplated and constructed. The creativity of each course as well as the play on flavours all worked very well and I liked how everything came together. It's quite clear that a lot of love and passion was put into the restaurant as a whole and not just in the food.

This will definitely not disappoint especially as Principe is such a different restaurant in Tainan. Fantastic for a special occasion or when you feel like indulging in the foodie within you!

I look forward to dining here again in future! =D
So amazing. Happy V Day 💕
We went there on New Year's Eve. Awesome experience, and the waiters were really nice as well ! The Chef came at the end to discuss with us. 10/10, it was perfect, we recommend to everyone !

reviews.text:
Don’t know how to express how much do I like this place’s buffet breakfast, not a big scale buffet but everything is on point, the most impressive thing is the Tainan food, beef soup, buns, braised pork rice, the drinks, unique and delicious.

We can choose our main course in “9 plates box”, Japanese ones is the best if you’re not a vegetarian, they have western vegetarian options and my friend said it’s not bad.

Choose their breakfast option if you stay at Provintia Hotel

The large buffet restaurant on the top floor of the hotel! It has a nice view from the windows around. The embellishment here is very great! Since the table is wide and the couch is soft, the cozy and casual ambiance makes the experience excellent!
Their courses are really good, moderate in portion and delectable in taste. While the price is fairly moderate, the restaurant provides much delicacy that are not commonly found elsewhere. Other dishes like bread soup, fruit or dessert are also delicious. Their service is prompt, so that one can enjoy the fresh made food with well selected ingredients.
It is truly a nice place for gathering of colleagues or friends. As it is not far from the train station, it is convenient for visitors to have a scrumptious meal downtown in this great restaurant! Very recommended!

Nice restaurant on the top floor of the hotel. Being refined, the dining environment and ambience of the restaurant is really relaxing and welcoming. Set menu, an entrée and salad buffet alongside is served here. I order 5 oz grilled filet with pepper sauce & prawn and scallops. The filet was grilled just right! It tastes so tender and juicy! Spaghetti, risotto, noodles, soups and breads are served at salad bar. Reservation is recommended.
Old School Western style restaurant, serves one of the best steak I've ever had. The decor is old school nostalgia with a touch of modern accent. Lovely dining atmosphere and friendly staff.

Visited on Jun 18. Spent about 2500 TWD for two persons.

Food and service definitely not up to hotel standards. The dining environment is decent, more like a semi-buffet setting.

Ordered the most expensive item on menu (should be), ribeye and lobster, but ended up both protein are substandard. The steak was supposed to be medium, but it was way under and it’s between rare and medium rare…. For the lobster, it was totally mushy so you know it’s frozen for quite some time….

Heard from one of the dinners said that the salad bar is mostly the same with their morning service, means they haven’t put much thought into the menu.

The only commendable item is the beef soup, which is Tainan’s stable hearty comfort food, the rest are really not that good at all.

On the service side, they probably have the least welcoming staff on reception that day, stone cold tone and not even a shed of smile.

I’m sure there are many better options in town for the same price range. Don’t waste your money.

Food rating is 4.5 stars for taste but service is 1 star for lack of training n some attitude!
We visited for lunch on Wed Feb 12; ordered some dim sum, stir fry Vege n rice noodle w beef 乾炒牛河粉 plus some turnip cakes to take home. I have been here before n Today food is kind of not as consistent: stir fry Vege was overcooked; charsiu pastry has thicker skin  n noodle plate has so little beef that it is so pathetic (crumbled 5 little pieces in a plate of noodle that charges $400NT. The worst is service!
When the noodle arrived, I was anxious to scoop it but disappointed that there is no beef so I asked the waitress. She politely replied there must be some in the bottom but then a man in the suit (supervisor?) jumped in n we told him. He immediately used the chopsticks to dig into the plate, flipping them n looked for beef then keep saying there r some.... N its same color so hard to find. Yet followed by saying have u had this dish before? Now I am upset, I have travelled half the world n ordered this where ever I get a chance...!
Then my friend said not even 5 pieces r found n the supervisor flipped n found some, said here they are.

In such class of restaurant, I would expect the supervisor to say ”I m sorry you r not satisfying, can I do sth about it. Take the dish into the kitchen n go flip it there, .... NOT at our table n please do not ever ask yr guests have you ever had this. At the end, w so few meat, he said ” our beef r import from US so it is expensive!”  I guess I should return to eat beef in US cos it's less than what we give to homeless in such class of restaurant in Taiwan! We tried to be pleasant to the waitress n enjoy our lunch, we walked past the supervisor who didn't greet us n gave us attitude upon our departure.

You might be famous n reputable but with this kind of arrogance n service, I will not return n neither my friends.

It serves famous shrimp rolls, milk fish congee, milk fish sausages, braised pork rice, and other various seafood dishes. Gourmets are advised to come here if they intend to experience the charming  local culture and cuisine in Tainan. Pay a visit. Ha....

It's like boiled/steamed and drizzled with their homemade braised minced pork. Something truly unique I've not tried anywhere else. The fried rolls were really good too, 真材实料, even the seafood cake, was filled with chunky bits of prawn and squid, not just seafood-flavoured flour paste.

It was impressive how he could nod or provide a slight hand gesture and the staff would respond promptly and professionally.

The teppanyaki dinner was nothing short of perfection. Each course was presented at an impeccable pace, allowing us to savor the delightful array of delicacies. The flavors were exquisite, and it was evident that great care and creativity went into the preparation of every dish.

I would also like to commend the support staff for their impeccable service. They engaged in mindful conversations without ever interrupting our experience, striking a perfect balance between attentiveness and discretion. A special mention goes to Ella, who took extra care to explain each course in English and patiently answered all our questions. Her dedication greatly enhanced our dining experience.

The rave reviews about ROBINS at Silks Palace are indeed well-deserved. Our visit confirmed that this is a must-visit destination for anyone seeking a remarkable culinary adventure. I highly recommend making reservations to anyone who hasn't yet experienced the magic of your restaurant.

Thank you once again for providing such a memorable evening. We look forward to returning for another exceptional meal in the near future.

Please share this message with Chef Lee and his staff who deserve recognition.

I haved a great lunch at this restaurant, the atmosphere was great the food was right. Aside of Teppanyaki there are various of cold dishes, salad, fruit and dessert selection. Service was great, staff are kind and supper friendly. Ranee was gentle and give us warm service. Definitely worth to come here.

We were here for lunch on a weekday. The server and chef were friendly and attentive. Salad bar featured a good variety of dishes and dessert bar offered one of the nicest financiers I had ever had.

The abalone was the star of the course! It was carefully prepared, tender with texture, flavourful and juicy!

Salad bar is fresh.  Onion soup is tasty.  We order not the most expensive meat but somehow i think it is not impressive in term of taste and texture.  The French dessert cart is cute,  others dessert is just good to look but taste so so. With such price level,  I would expect better quality. Overall service is excellent!

Also, the restaurant runs out of things frequently when you want that one the most on that day.

The only thing the consistent, alas, is the beer. But I wish you would use the same style glasses so nobody feels unsure if they got a true amount of beer.

reviews.text:
Birthday dinner at Liang-Liang was absolutely delightful! The ambiance was very comfortable and relaxing, and the service was exceptional, with the warm welcoming and the staffs explaining each dish with passion.
Among the array of delicious offerings, my favorite was the first dish, the "Crab." This soup with crab meat and steamed egg was velvety smooth, a true delight with every bite. And the fourth dish, “Oyster of Qigu,” was equally impressive, with a foam infused with the fragrance of perilla flowers atop a bowl of rich and flavorful orzo pasta, not only satisfying the visual and gustatory senses, but also telling a story of how the established fish farming industry shaped the palate of the Tainan natives.
Also. don't forget to reserve the dessert "Sugar Ball” to conclude your wonderful dinner on a high note!
Overall, this dinner left a lasting impression on me, and I look forward to returning to more of their fantastic dishes. Highly recommend for date nights and other important occasions.

If I had to describe the experience of Liang Liang 2.0 in one word, it would be “balance”. Dual male/female chefs bring childlike joy and sophisticated restraint together in the plate, the menu, and the environment. In a town of ancient foods craved by generations of Taiwanese, Liang Liang 2.0 is a welcome taste for the new gen of globally and locally minded foodies. 10/10
Can’t love more

The restaurant, run by a young couple, originally sold some of their favorite meals, but has now changed to a set menu. You must order online to dine. The following are the meals that were tasted that day: 🐟Fried eel balls 🍗Silk-bone chicken wings 🥖Homemade ciabatta ｜Snake fish/garlic/anchovy cream 🐠Squid ｜bergamot/Kyoto water vegetables/radish 🥬Cauliflower rolls ｜Sealed chicken combs/Spanish bacon Sausage/Spaghetti/Yuzu Pepper (I’m so curious about the flavor, I couldn’t wait to start it after hearing the introduction, no photos🤣) 🦪Abalone|Japanese seaweed/Abalone Mushroom/Horseradish 🥔Jerusalem Artichoke｜Red Oolong Tea/Sea Cucumber/Dried Scallops 🐑Way Goat Saddle 🍓Limited Season Sugar Ball: A beautiful and delicious dessert✨ 🧁Feinan Snow｜Chocolate Tart｜French Fudge 🍵Herb Tea Compared with restaurants of the same level in Taipei, the prices here are quite affordable, the food is exquisite and not sloppy at all, and it has been warmly received by the staff. reviews.text: Delicious food and wonderful hosts! The salad is amazingly refreshing. The tempeh green curry is super fragrant and hearty. If you have a craving for Indian food but also want to keep your healthy diet, this place is just perfect. Highly recommend and please support them if you are in Tainan!

Such an amazing restaurant with a wonderful ethos!! We have ordered online from this place so many times but decided to go in person today, we got chatting to the owner and he is so passionate and knowledgeable about health. The food is delicious every time, and it tastes even better knowing how much care went into it and how high quality the ingredients are. Definitely will be returning:)

A very cozy environment where you can enjoy the taste of Indian curries. The prices are reasonable and most of the dishes are perfect for health conscious persons. The diner provides many different flavors of Indian style curry dishes - different from the Taiwanese or Japanese curry.
Not salty, the curry flavor of each dish tastes slightly different.
For the eggplant curry, it tasted almost creamy - highly recommended.
The vagetable/beans in curry help balance the spicy taste with their sweetness, so if you chose the dish with more vagetable in it, the spicy level could be stronger-if you like it hot!
Special hot sauce is also provided by the owner, which is really good (hot).

Freshly baked Indian pancake smells almost ceramel sweet. Pull apart the pancake with your hands, feel the warm and fluffy texture, dip the pancake into curry, wrap the curry, or eat it like pizza - with layers of curry on it - anyways, you'll feel happy when you're eating.

The owner is cheerful and welcoming.
Price reasonable, dining space is small and clean. Business is good, almost always busy, so reservation is recommended.
Overall, it's a small, warm place, serves great Indian curry, and Indian music - the latter is free.

reviews.text: This restaurant was overall a wonderful experience, with delicious food with a good flavour balance. We ordered the cucumber & martini, the signature fried tofu, the lions mane skewers, and the yellow curry. The first two dishes were perfect, with perfect flavours and textures. The tofu was soft inside and super crispy on the outside with a delectable sauce, and the cucumber was crisp and tasty. The skewers were perfect taste and texture wise, but were served quite cold, which was not to my liking. The flavour of the yellow curry sauce was great, but the vegetables inside were not cooked properly, all overcooked and in too large chunks, and there was way too many lemongrass pieces that could not be eaten, which made eating it a bit harder.

Vegetarian restaurants primarily selling stir fried dishes. Has a private room as well
Okonomiyaki - One of the best I've had, crispy, fragrant and flavorful even without the mayonnaise.
The 小炒 stir fry was quite delicious too.
The stir fried eel is a pass though. The mushrooms and cabbage don't really mimick the concept of eel well to be honest.
Despite it being in Tainan, the savory dishes are not sweet, so it's a plus for those who do not like their savory dishes having a sweet taste.

went there for dinner tonight, we will not go back and we will tell everyone about that. everything is kinda sour. and since this is the first time we went, we don't even know we got a wrong dish. ordered the savory stinky tofu and got a hot and sour soup instead and it cost $50 less. and they even start cleaning the restaurant while we are still eating. they definitely win the trophy of being the worst restaurant that I went during my 10 days trip in Taiwan
Very tasty! There is an English menu if you can’t speak or read Mandarin.

Great vegetarian restaurant. Beautiful plating and atmosphere and clearly the establishment focuses on balance of flavors. The cucumber and crispy skin tofu were a standout and the skewers were also good but the mushroom element could have been warmer. The yellow curry flavour was delicious but I found the bits of lemongrass difficult as they could not really be eaten.

reviews.text:
07 July 2024
09 July 2024

Come to have dinner at this restaurant while staying Shangri-La Tainan.
I think this is the tallest building in Tainan

Food
Their food tastes are pretty decent, 1 or 2 dishes that are pretty plain. But overall, it is ok.

Service
Communication is still a problem here as they can't speak English. Only a couple of waiter that can speak English.

Actually the service is pretty good except on the second visit it looks like they are sort of waiter or maybe the table next to me also a big group.

Food comes out does not come in order.
Where as appertizers should come first, but they come out their main dishes first. And in the middle of the main dishes, come the appertizers.
Almost at the end of our dinner, here  comes the soup.

I think most high-end restaurants should be pretty strict about the order of the dishes, which should be first and so on.

Atmosphere
Look at the view, superb.
The food was delicious. Thank you, Lulu, for taking our picture with the Tainan city view.

What a lovely experience!!.  Food was delicious. The crispy pork pie was the best. Could have eaten 2 of them.
Beautiful setting. Beautiful view. Service was awesome! Loved the place.

Chinese dishes are nice, with some local tainan choices. Wine is available. The dining room is large with view over the city; each time we came it was rather empty. In compare to what is available in the city, Shanghai Pavilion is a safe bet !

No menu was given after sitting at table for close to 5mins. We were thirsty so ordered for a pot of tea Oolong tea from the wait staff in coat (still, no menu was given to us at this point) but did not mentioned have Long Jing which eventually we ordered AGAIN for Long Jing after we requested for menu (which does not taste like Long Jing more like black tea) Food was average, nothing to shout about. Roasted duck and recommended chef main dish need advance booking, else not available though it's listed on menu (only for the regulars i suppose) Light quite dim to read menu if you were sitting away from window table. Steamed fish was ordered and was seen left at counter table and not served to us for solid 5mins. In my mind i hope that fish is not ours, as must have been cold. Unfortunately, it's indeed ours. Accomodation stay was good, good experience. Breakfast was same for past 2 days though.

Will not be my 1st choice or at least my business trip if include accomodation, with concern on dinner experience. (this time is family trip, no point making hoo-ha about)

1. When we first arrived the chief staff tried to send us away and  tell us come next time until we insisted to wait for a table.

For a Michelin star, I was not impressed and didn't have a wow effect.

Something strang, you have to buy your vegetables first at the entrance like in supermarket and pay it. Then go to your table and order your food, then coock your vegetables in a hot pot.
The value for money is okayish.
It's a popular place and apparently you need to queue... it's not worth to queue.  I got in without waiting.

Beef hotpot was good despite the Michelin. But it definitely was not a WOW.

Light delicate broth. Brisket and tendons pre stewed soft. Beautiful decor, 4 floors of tables. Allowing much more people to get a table without a lengthy wait.

I've had better.

I visited the old A-Yu beef hotpot quite often, this is my first time to visit their new shop, much bigger and modern. The hotpot soup and the beef are still good, one of my best Tainan beef hotpot so far. Don’t miss their braised beef rice, you can take it for free at the self serve bar.

Get here early is my advice. Or at least send one person to line up first. Our taxi took us here at 4:07 PM when the store opens at 5 PM. There was already 10 people in line before us. By the time it hit 4:50PM there was probably 80 people in line behind us.

There is all you can eat braised pork on white rice. The freshly slaughtered sliced on site Beef is extremely tender and delicious and relatively well priced. highly enjoyable, and definitely recommend it to tourists and locals alike.
Heard this was famous and the hot pot lived up to the hype. The beef is farm to table fresh and delicious. One of the best shabu shabu I've ever had and all you can eat lu rou fun.

This was hands down one of the best food experiences in Taiwan.

Sit out on the street, is lively and the food is amazing.
good job aa

After watching the fireworks at the orthodox Luermen Thean Hou Temple, I was lucky enough to find a nearby late-night snack with high reviews. There were many people at the scene. I ordered the Korean dry noodles with a tumbler, which was delicious. The signature roasted pork omelette was praised by all 👍. The pot-roasted pasta was quite satisfactory and the meal was served very quickly. I recommend it to foodies who like late-night snacks.

There were a lot of people. Only the seats outside were dark and mosquito-infested. Many tables were empty, but we were asked to ask them to clear the tables🥹 The soufflé was not very tasty, and the kimchi omelette also had a weird taste. The roasted pork toast did not add eggs, so it was a bit expensive and not very delicious. The minced pork noodles were ordinary instant noodles. I added soy sauce to it and it was still edible. I don’t know why there were so many people, but I regretted not going to the next door where I usually eat for a midnight snack🤣

I accidentally found this "Micro Late Night" on the delivery platform. The soup is amazing, with many ingredients, rich and delicious. It is very similar to the "old" KFC soup with potatoes. Unlike many thick soups on the market that are very thin and lacking in ingredients. The tumbler dry noodles are also very delicious. There are eggs, meat slices, rice cakes, and fish plates. But if you don't like spicy food, please consider it. There are extra pickles.

The pork leg rice is like pork rice, more than 2/3 is fat, and the meat is small, really like pork rice, but it is not braised. At the price of 95 yuan...the cartilage bento is okay. The side dishes are more of a meal type, with relatively few vegetables.

reviews.text:
Our family came here for a birthday celebration and the food was so delicious! The set menu was so amazing with some Taiwanese dishes I’ve never tried before. They were all beautifully prepared with very fresh quality ingredients. The salad was so refreshing! The soups were so decadent and the best soups I’ve had. No matter how full I was, I couldn’t stop drinking more soup!!

The service was excellent. The servers were never far away and changed plates, provided wet hand towels throughout the meal.

Apparently, this is where chefs eat, so that says a lot!!

Shin Yeh offers an exceptional experience of traditional Taiwanese cuisine in a refined setting. The menu boasts a variety of authentic dishes, each prepared with meticulous attention to detail.

Highlights:
•	Signature Dishes: The shrimp with pineapple features perfectly battered and fried shrimp complemented by a delightful sweet mayo glaze. The crispy-fried fresh oysters are another standout, offering a juicy and flavorful bite. The three-cup chicken, rich in soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, chilis, and basil, is a flavorful testament to traditional Taiwanese flavors.  ￼
•	Service: The staff is attentive and accommodating, with many members proficient in English, enhancing the dining experience for international guests.  ￼
•	Atmosphere: The restaurant’s ambiance is clean and welcoming, providing a comfortable environment to enjoy a meal.  ￼

Considerations:
•	Popularity: Given its reputation, the restaurant can become busy, especially during peak hours. It’s advisable to make reservations in advance to ensure a seamless experience.
•	Pricing: While the quality of food justifies the prices, some dishes may be on the higher end. However, the generous portions and exceptional flavors offer good value for money.

In conclusion, Shin Yeh provides a memorable journey through Taiwanese culinary traditions, combining exquisite flavors with excellent service and a pleasant atmosphere. It’s a worthwhile destination for both newcomers and enthusiasts of Taiwanese cuisine.

Found this place online and cross checked it with Google reviews and i still wasn't too sure what to expect. My partner and I dressed up and came here for date night. We were quite overdressed. It's a big taiwanese restaurant that seems to cater for all groups- families, business meetings over meals, and couples. All are welcome. The staff are efficient and helpful, despite my limited Mandarin. The food was really outstanding. We especially enjoyed the braised pork belly and the stir fried scallops. I wish I'd ordered the oyster omelette. Will have to come back. This place does elevated local dishes in an undeniable way. Excellent

Every dish is awesome❗
Big tables available for more than 10 people

Our relatives brought us to this Taiwanese restaurant in Taipei, because it's one of their favorites.

This certainly didn't disappoint, every dish is delicious and certainly very authentic, as approved by the local relatives, service was excellent too, serving was fast and very attentive.

The pig liver was the best I have tried, I don't usually like it, but this is so delicious. The fried oysters were super yummy too!

reviews.text:
28/3/25

1019am, I started to join the long queue.

1033am, I managed to get a queue ticket. The counter lady even asks which language menu, nationality I am from, to better accommodate to customer spoken language. Making it way easier to order, understand the menu.

1045am, they open. Within 5-10mins, I am being ushered in by this cute robot as shown in the video.

Upon confirming the order via QR code, you have the option to get the staff to reconfirm the order with you, choose whether you would like the dessert to be served concurrently or later.

Did not have to wait long for the food. Within 10 minutes. My first dish had arrived.

The crab roe and pork xiao long bao is as usual. High standard with no flaws.

The pork rice wrap gives a local authentic taste.

The steamed beef soup may look unassuming, but man, the broth taste was heavenly, especially on a rainy cold weather.

The dessert, must order, dark chocolate dimpling is to DIE FOR!
Bitter aftertaste that aids in clearing the palette of oily pork.

Oh, the tea is FREE WITH ENDLESS TOPUP. Perfect to wash down the throat.

Want to shout out to the ultra attentive trainee staff anne, I am sorry, unsure how to type your mandarin name fully within that few seconds of interaction.

She was very friendly, prompt service upon asking to top up the tea and even automatically top up whenever customer tea cup is emptied. Even gave me directions on where to locate the nearest restroom (toilet is outside and not inside the restraining) when I make the enquiry. Though I am unable to see her face through the face mask, but the eye smile and friendliness make it super welcoming to customers dining in.

Hope she can be a confirmed staff for the taipei 101 branch soon. She has set a high bar for others to emulate.

Table 26-1, 1045am-12pm.

From a Singaporean, Singapore, who has dined in Singapore outlet, Din Tai Fung multiple times. The service standard is paler compared to the service received in Taipei 101. Taipei 101 outlet all staff ought to be recognised for their excellent service and perhaps, an increment in their salary? 😁

Will love to dine in again whenever I drop by Taipei.

Hope Taipei 101 Din Tai Fung outlet can expand their seatings.  I only manage to dine in the second attempt.
First attempt the queue was too long. 😅

1/2025
A Taiwanese cultural experience.  If you go, you must try. Yes, there are a plethora of Taiwanese restaurants to try but this is one end of the spectrum you need to experience.  Reservations, if accepted,  are highly recommended. It just depends. I loved the atmosphere and food was very delicious.  I must say though, I really enjoyed the use of tech, especially with my host who sat me. Stop by, it's worth the wait, and I ordered as much as I could eat off the menu. 😉😋🤙✌️

Good juicy pork dumplings. Eggplant is so fit. Stir fried sugar peas are tender. The peanut sauce noodles are too spicy for me even though I ordered the non spicy version. The deep fried pork chop fried rice however, is okay. The deep fried pork chop is definitely a bit dried and oily. We took the reservation number at 5:30pm and the expected wait is 60 to 85 min. We got in at 7pm. Yes the food is good but personally don’t think it worths the wait - obviously can shop around and come back at the intended time. Price reasonably.

A highly recommended restaurant, located on the dining floor of Taipei 101. The establishment has one Michelin star. Entering the restaurant, you can see how the dim sum is prepared in the transparent kitchen. The food is clean and extremely tasty, and the service is amazing. The price is very reasonable for this level. It is worth visiting even with the lengthy line.

It’s definitely worth the wait and a must visit in Taipei.

Without exaggeration, the best xiaolongbao I’ve ever eaten. We tried the classic ones filled with pork and the ones filled with shrimps.

The classic ones are much better regarding taste. It was juicy due to the light broth and the meat filling wasn’t fatty and was well balanced. The dough was also not too thick.

I also loved the fried rice with shrimp. It was so delicious, flavorful and lightweight. The custard bun was also so good and not too sweet! 👍
The sweet sour soup was regarding taste nothing special.

Additionally the service was excellent, as they were quite friendly and attentive. The staff was pouring/refilling tea in the cups regularly at each table.

reviews.text:
Excellent meal here, very interesting take on Taiwanese Chinese cuisine.

Our family liked every dish we ordered. Standout were the Yam with Pork ribs that was done in a meatloaf fashion, and the sour fish soup. All outstanding in their own right.

They had special rice with Japan furikake and seaweed for kids as a default, which the kids liked.

Atmosphere is up-market casual, not stuffy .

Amazing traditional Taiwanese food
Totally love it
See you again
@jonathanviatge
They offer modern Taiwanese cuisine with small portion of food. Reservation is recommended for weekend.

This is a local Taiwanese restaurant which is a hidden gem. The chicken is flavourful (we wondered where the source of their poultry is from - little fat and has those countryside tastes) and well presented. I recommend the big portion because the smaller amount (which we ordered came with too many bones - unless you are a bone person). The tofu on the hot iron plate is also very nice when served hot; mixed with their local sauce enhances the taste. I must recommend the pineapple drink (you seldom see me recommending drinks); it's incredible! - cooling and taste a bit sweet, excellent to have with your meal. Go by the jar, which is cheaper than a cup, and it's enough to be shared by 3-4 persons.

Highly recommended if you want to have authentic and affordable Taiwanese food.

All the food items we ordered were delicious, especially the fried egg, chicken and top shell soup.

We were pleasantly surprised on how fast they served even though we ordered many.

Staff were friendly and prompt. Cozy environment for gathering. Very reasonable price too.
