reviews.text:
Their rice noodles was so good!  I never had such good rice noodles in my life!

Their service was very nice too。

We had such a good experience there, we would visit them again if We come back to Taiwan.😋

We had the Mei tasting menu and it was a good experience. Reasonable price, a lot of courses. All of the flavours were very delicate and well balanced. With the exception of one dish which the waiter explained was specifically designed to be very strong. Good presentation too.

Service was pretty slow and I had to remind them if ordered a drink after waiting 30 min without getting anything.

I selected this one as it features some dishes that require delicate work that’s not commonly available elsewhere. The interior is clean and comfy.
A few dishes require reservations and its dining reservations also ask your credit card guarantee when you try online!
All dishes are fresh and look nice by appearance. The taste is light, not too salty at all, so the flavor is presented quite originally. Each dish was introduced properly and the waitresses did check frequently our demand. Was a great dining experience!

A Michelin starred restaurant serving traditional Taiwanese. We went for their set menu which included a few of their signatures. In general, it fell short of my expectations. The food was of a good quality but it didn't wow, neither in taste nor in food presentation. I did enjoy the Roasted Suckling Pig which was served in 3 ways - crackling skin (1 pc each only), meat and ribs, shredded meat in Gua Bao. The traditional fried bee hoon was delish too, so basic, so simple but yummy, using their local bee hoon that's more bouncy in texture. The dessert was also interesting, first time having grass jelly in pure liquid form instead of the solidified jelly and to have it with crushed peanuts added a different dimension. I was disappointed though that they didn't ask about nut allergy, not that I have it but I expected that of a Michelin star restaurant charging S$160 per pax.

Reservations required and some dishes require advance ordering too.

Exquisite dining experience at this upscale restaurant that focuses on traditional Taiwanese cuisine. All of the food items were presented meticulously, and seasoned & cooked perfectly. Friendly and efficient service helped to round out a perfect evening!

reviews.text:
Tucked in an actual alley, Red Alley Bistro is a hidden gem. The lady running the place speaks a little english but her kind and welcoming gesture makes you feel instantly comfortable. Note that you’ll need to pay when placing your order.

I tried the Taiwanese salty pork and sweet and sour diced chicken—both were absolutely delicious, with authentic flavors that hit the spot. The passion fruit green tea is a standout and an absolute must-try, perfectly balancing sweetness and refreshing flavors.

Hidden gem in the alley own by a humble lady. She tried her best to accommodate us although one group reserve the spot but did not turn up for more then 10 minutes. They came 15 minutes after we sat down.

Their signature dishes is good. We order chicken, beef and pork. I would think their pork and beef dishes are the best.

Do not forget to add egg for TWD30. Worth it to eat with their food.

Please do not reserve your spot if you came late. Space are limited, but they are nice to reserve, hoping you will arrive

Super tasty home made food. The couple are super nice and although they can't speak English will try their best. The fish we had was amazing and tasty. Prices are also super reasonable. Beware the place is closed on Monday and Thursday.

This is the best food I’ve had in a loooooong time!
I have not been reviewing many places lately and I haven’t felt the need to as I have not eaten many things that swept me off my feet, but this place did just that! Red Alley Bistro made me remember just how appreciative one should be about having amazing food in hidden little gems such as this one! Although it isn’t in the fanciest setting nor is it the most comfortable frame, it is very welcoming and the food is PHENOMENAL!!
We had the Sweet and Sour Chicken and the Salty Pork and they were so delicious that I wish everyone would have the pleasure to eat here at least once in their lives!
All dishes come with a soup, vegetables, white rice and we ordered an extra soy egg that was also pretty good! Last and not least, the Passion Fruit Teas (one green, one black) were also delicious, but we had a slight preference for the green tea version.
All in all, if you don’t know what to eat in Taipei and want to have an experience you’ll remember, come here!
Our only regret is that we found this place on our last day in Taiwan or else we would have become regulars!

What a lovely restaurant! Be careful to watch where it is, almost missed it. It is indeed in an alley way. Also, make sure to close the door behind you to keep the AC in. Absolutely delicious food and the staff were kind and efficient. Would go here again, would suggest to all of my friends!
It’s a little small and it’s no Michelin star environment, but it’s charming for an alley way restaurant!

Red Alley Bistro.vicinity: No. 3號, Lane 171, Hanzhong Street, Wanhua District

reviews.text: We had a business dinner at MUME. I have to say I was so surprised by the different dishes and flavors, you can clearly tell the homage to the various cuisines and food cultures throughout the menu (duck- French, pasta- Italian, fish- Scandinavian, ceviche- Peruvian etc etc) this was a real celebration of global gastronomy and it took us on a journey around the world and back to Taiwan - loved every dish. Presentation is amazing, flavors are bold yet balanced. Thank you for taking us on this amazing journey. If you’re in Taiwan- this is A MUST visit.

The service here was excellent, and the food was good, though not particularly memorable. The restaurant leans toward American-Western fine dining. I visited for their Valentine’s special, which was a course set with three wine pairings for 6,500 each.

While the experience was pleasant, the cocktails and whisky selection were average and didn’t stand out. Overall, it’s a decent choice for a special occasion, but not one I’d rush back to.

I had the pleasure of experiencing truly exceptional customer service at this Michelin-starred restaurant.

After another group complained about their table near the door, we were graciously moved to the entrance without our consent. How generous!

Apparently, the "exceptional customer service" only applied to the other table, as they were quickly accommodated.
To top it off, we were seated right next to clothes hanging, like we were dining in a dressing room.
Nothing says fine dining like enjoying your meal next to a rack of jackets.

On a positive note, the sourdough and duck was quite good, but the other food was just fair. This is definitely not what I expected from a Michelin-starred establishment!

An innovative fine dining that positions itself as a fusion restaurant. Spends much more effort at the visual presentation that is an feast to the eye than to the palate. Taste is either too bland or too heavily leaning on local flavor with chilly and oil. Wine pairing and cocktail pairing were quite disappointing: was served two sb similar for the starters, one nz gewurztraminer for the fish, an overpowering orange wine for the squid, and a Bordeaux for the beef. Cocktail didn't do too well either: a sweet pineapple flavored for beef, a sweet one for the fish? Service was impeccable though.
Finally one of these fusion western-Taiwanese restaurants bring fresh foods without them being bland. Good wine pairing too and very good service. Drinks were also top notch

reviews.text:
Line out the door and around the corner 20 minutes before opening, but well worth the wait. The line moves quickly and there is plenty of seating.

Ordering is easy, but you need to know what you want before you get to the counter since they move people through very quickly. I heard staff speaking English and Japanese in addition to Mandarin.

The food was really good and comes out quickly. Definitely worth a try.

The food was good but not worth the hour long wait. We were in line at around 8AM and the line was wrapped around the block - it was unfortunately the weekend. The ordering process was very smooth so the line was moving at a slow, but steady pace.
We enjoyed hot soy milk. The salty soy milk was ok. We liked the crunchy donut stick.

Be prepared to queue up as soon as you exit Shandao Temple Station Exit 4. The queue moves quickly, though. We arrived at 11:35 AM and found the queue to be quite long, with around 200 people in line. We queued for approximately 1.5 hours. Some items were already sold out, but we were still able to order most of the items we wanted. Service is very fast though once you get in the order line.

The food is inexpensive and delicious, and I thoroughly enjoyed all of it. However, after several bites, I noticed that the flavors became somewhat repetitive.

Overall, it’s probably worth the wait to experience the food and atmosphere once, but I wouldn’t recommend going back again due to the long wait time.

This was another soy milk place that I was recommended that I tried during the trip. The venue is inside a shopping mall/arcade and is upstairs in the food court area. You will know it is for that place as the queue was outside surrounding the building. Our waiting time was about 40 mins around 12pm. There is a menu with pictures so that made it easy to order. We had savory and sweet soy milk, lots of different pastry and buns with fried dough and egg which was a perfectly savory, oily, and good for breakfast. I personally preferred the savory  soy milk at the other view but overall it was a good hearty breakfast.

- No matter what time you go, I think you’ll hit a line here. But being Taipei, everything moves fast. We were in line, ordered, found a table, and ate within 1 hour around 10AM on a Tuesday. The line sometimes wraps around the block so make sure you find the end. This store  is located upstairs in a food court (I felt bad for the other empty restaurants)  and they are not patient at all when it’s time to order. So it would be best to use the menus in line and online to look up what you want and order before you get there. The first person does milks only - this is where you get your milk to go, soy milk, salty milk, rice milk. The second does the food orders then you pay at the end. Cash only. Finding a table can be difficult but we managed to snag one quickly. Table for hot sauces and chopsticks. Unfortunately they didn’t have straws. Now down to the food - coming from the US, I was baffled about why people were raving about soy milk of all things and after trying this place, I understood the hype. The salty soy milk was nothing like I’ve had before.. with the addition of the fried dough, it gave it a texture that just uplifted the whole thing. We also got the fried dough, egg pancake, and the egg wrap. Could have skipped the fried dough but it was nice to have more to dip in the salty milk. TBH everything was pretty oily so if this is where you start your day, might want to find some non fried foods for the rest of the day. We got a cold soy milk to wash everything down with and that was the perfect ending to this amazing breakfast.

Fuhang Soy Milk.vicinity: 2樓, No. 108, Section 1, Zhongxiao East Road, Zhongzheng District

reviews.text:
[Review for the original take-out location]
Honestly, pretty disappointing considering all the hype.

I came with my friend at around 7 pm and got the xiao long bao, shrimp fried rice, siu mai, and spicy wontons.

We waited about 30 minutes for our food and then walked about 5 minutes to a park nearby to eat. We didn't even wait that long to eat, and none of the food was hot.

The soup dumplings were cold, and the rest were lukewarm. The fried rice and siu mai taste pretty average and similar to what you can find at other restaurants. I will admit, the spicy wontons were absolutely amazing. I could eat that with anything and it'll taste good.

Overall, for the amount we paid, I feel like you could find MUCH better food around Taipei. I've never been to the actual Din Tai Fung restaurants since those are a 1-2+ hour wait, but I'm sure they're much better. We paid homage to the original location, but I wouldn't come back.

The original store of Din Tai Fung, by Yang Bing-yi and his wife, Lai Pen-mei in 1972. They still maintain this stall for iconic reason. This is ground zero and birthplace of DTF. No dine in, only takeaway. If u are a DTF fan, this is the must for a visit to absorb the vibes and history. Just for that.
For proper dining experience walk 3 mins to the nearest DTF restaurant and immerse yourself in a hour long Q before getting a table. Plan ahead.

It's almost tastes the same as Din Tai Fung in my home country or other countries. It's good but not that wow and quite pricey in my home country compared to other dimsum place with the same flavor imo.
But my brother really likes their salted egg buns and can't get over it in Taiwan.
15-20mins waiting, they got fireplace outside during our visit in freezing winter.

The original establishment is now a Togo inky store in 赤峰街.

The cucumber salad was not as amazing per my memory. We end up letting the cucumber marinade overnight, a tad better. The soup dumplings were awesome even after an hour.

20 mins wait even with just takeout .

Great for take out. This is the original Din Tai Fung, so if you are a fan this is a must.
Founded in 1972, DTF is known worldwide, and this historical place was fun to see. Try some other things than Xiao Long Bao, even if they nearly are a must..
Michelin awarded, what is their secret you might wonder. Great flavours, made the same way every time.

Din Tai Fung Xinyi Branch - TAKEOUT ONLY.vicinity: No. 194號, Section 2, Xinyi Road, Da’an District

This branch is as good as the others. The food quality is consistent. The service is fast and efficient  the staff are gentle and smiling. The food experience is excellent.
There's lots of people and if you don't go early the waiting time can go up to 2 hours.
However, it is highly recommended

The YouTube folks hype up the food here, but it doesn’t live up to it.
Mediocre food—a big disappointment for us. We expected more. The prices are quite steep, and there are countless places with better food at a lower price.

That said, the service and queue system were pretty good.

Food: 3/5
Service: 5/5
Environment: 5/5
Atmosphere: 4/5
Overall Rating: 4/5

Review: A lot of locals and tourists hype for this restaurant. We came here before lunch time, at 11.25am. There was already a lot of people, but we got our queue and the estimated wait time was 10 - 15 minutes. The staff gave us a place to put our luggage bags since we just checked out of our hotel 2 MRT stations away, and went to explore the mall around. Good thing we arrived early, because when we arrived back 10 minutes later, the wait time had become 30 - 45 minutes.

We were seated at 11.35am, and placed our orders via the QR code provided. The staff were really friendly, and guided us to our table. They even provided an area for us to put our bags in a small bin! Each person was given hot tea for free, bowls, ginger and soy sauce and vinegar as well. The food here isn't cheap. We got their famous pork Xiaolongbao, ordered 12 for NT$336. Also tried their shredded pork fried rice for NT$250.

The xiaolongbao was kinda decent. They had a card showing the instructions on how to eat it. You're suppose to poke the bottom with a chopstick, letting the broth flow out and eat it with one bite. I didn't really like it that much, but it wasn't too bad. The fried rice was kinda a disappointment though. While it looked tasty, the taste just wasn't there. There wasn't enough flavouring, and too much spring onion. Could have used more soy sauce, so not a huge fan of it. The area was noisy too since all the tables were filled with people.

So, to me, it's not really worth the hype. It's basically Chinese food but more expensive. I'd have to say street food actually tastes better than this, but I'm not complaining about their really good service and environment!

I eat at this place every time I come to Taiwan. Food is top notch. Not cheap but not crazy either. They have many locations in big cities in Taiwan. Look their soup dumplings best. Also vegetables dishes very tender and minimal seasoning, just right

We had a 90 minute wait at lunchtime on a Friday. Downloaded the Din Tai Fung app so we could walk around and shop while waiting.

When we got our table, the waiter asked if we had pre-ordered, which we had not. This was not a problem, we were given time to order.

The food came very quickly, and was delicious. The xiao long bao were full of savoury flavour, stir fried vegetables were fresh and subtlely sweet, and the wontons were the best we had tried outside of Hong Kong.

Overall, a fantastic dining experience, and very much recommended

reviews.text: Din Tai Fung has an excellent reputation in Taipei, and the and the lines are usually long to eat here after my lunch here. I can understand why. The food was excellent and I particularly enjoyed the fried rice, soup, dumplings, and hot and sour soup. The server Fiona spoke excellent and  was particularly helpful as I attempted to navigate the menu. Pro tip: I arrived when this branch opened and had to wait only five minutes to be seated.

We come to 鼎泰豐 once a month almost, and their food is consistently excellent, their service is reliable and courteous, and their whole operations runs like clockwork.

This time, I ordered dishes we hadn’t tried before: lamb dumplings (turmeric coriander), and tofu puff glass noodle soup. Bother were great, as expected. Wife and kids ordered what we normally get. Whole dinner came to $2400, whereas we typically end around $1700 or so.
Top class Taiwanese dishes, with fantastic service. As a vegetarian I wish there were more choices, but nonetheless the food is excellently made, and always fresh.

Shrimp dumplings were tasty!!
Pork chop noodles: noodles itself were good, and I wish the pork could be more marinated, now it’s less tasty and less crunchy.
Service: excellent. Staff keep refilling tea for us.

Great food, great service.
Try the truffle dumplings, the spicy dumplings and the fried pork cutlet with stir fried rice. Great dishes.
The beef soup was ok, probably the only dish I wouldn’t order again.
I also bought the chili oil.
A must try!

reviews.text:
I am very disappointed in their famous dish of crab steam rice. The crab was horribly overcooked, and the crab roe tasted like "rubber." Sadly that I was busy talking with friends, the dish was eaten and too late to tell them of the bad quality. 👎
The crab looked ok, but the taste was bad. I struggled for a while to post cause I rarely made bad comments. But this restaurant really failed me cause I insisted on visiting and had high expectations before going.  That's not a good experience. 😕
Really appreciate the restaurant that gave us a table to celebrate Mother’s Day. The cuisines are nice, and their staffs give us quite warm hospitality. Highly recommended!
Refined Taiwanese/ 宜蘭 dishes, very unique and flavorful. Too bad that we were busy eating and didn’t get a chance to take some pictures of the dishes.

Must eat the Yilan shrimp and chicken gyoza (which are not actually dumplings), which are delicious dipped in white pepper. The pork tendon with garlic is also outstanding.

The sesame oil chicken rice is also incredibly delicious, just know that it is a lot of food so either come hungry or come in a group.

Impressive food, good service but quite pricey compared to other restaurant food.

Ordered:
1. Garlic shrimp (appetizer) 5/5
I love garlic, and this small shrimp with fried garlic is a perfect combo for me

2. Yilan style pork and cabbage casserole
(Best dishes-must order!)
It’s taste pretty simple yet rich and very flavourful. It has meat and vegetable also, a complete dish.

3. Caipo Egg
(Must order)
Caipo egg is the most dish you can find in any taiwan restaurant so I don’t think I will get surprised with this, but turn out this is the best caipo egg I’ve ever tried so far. Just that a bit downside is a bit too oily for me. Other than it’s perfect!

reviews.text:
My meal at Le Palais was truly exceptional. The duck, prepared in four distinct ways, was a revelation. It's safe to say it's set a very high bar for any future duck dishes I might encounter. It ruined me!  The tea infusions were also remarkable, offering a depth of flavor that was both surprising and delightful. And the dim sum? Exquisite, each piece a small masterpiece.
The service was also noteworthy, attentive without being intrusive. They are like mind reading ninjas!  I'm already contemplating a return visit, if only to experience that duck again. It was a memorable dining experience, and one that I would highly recommend.

The food here is good, but I would say at a one Michelin star level, maybe two. The flavors are good but lack a stand out factor that is truly three star worthy. Also, the kitchen forgot about one of our a la carte orders for 1h40min which is frankly unacceptable for a restaurant presenting at this level.

Ambiance was quite lovely. Food was perfect. As a solo diner I was not able to enjoy the specialties like Peking duck or roast pig. Service was outstanding especially Yoden who was attentive, helpful and friendly which made the experience much better for being solo. Dumplings, fried rice, spicy chicken and cabbage were delicious.

amazing vibe and unique and special service, started out great and also ended great but some of the dishes in the middle were not as good, you only remember the beginning and ending tho 😁

Standouts were baby duck and shrimp and lobster roll. The complementary tea was the best tea I’ve ever had in my life

*note: did not order a set menu

It’s a great experience visiting one of only 4 cantonese restaurants in the world thats been awarded with 3 michelin star. Service is on par, servicing staff are very knowledgeable in every single dish. Deco, atmosphere & vibe is on par. Food is great, i truly enjoy every single dish, especially ribs. However, i find most dishes lag the gastronomy touch to it. Dont get me wrong, traditional  cantonese cooking is definitely one of the best cuisine in the world, but to be at a 3 michelin star level, one would think it needs to be more then traditional.
Anyhow, i will still come visit this restaurant whenever im in taipei. Exceptional experience.

reviews.text:
Came for lunch with my in-laws before Lunar New Year and my return to Canada, a meal that carried both festive cheer and the unspoken pressure of making a good impression.

The dishes arrive at an almost alarming speed, as if the kitchen staff have been trained by an elite unit of culinary sprinters. The flavors are pleasant, balanced, and undeniably well-executed, but if you’re looking for a dish that whispers sweet nothings to your soul or ignites a passionate food epiphany, you may leave slightly unromanced. That being said, there’s nothing to fault, everything is enjoyable, just a touch… restrained.

Service is warm and attentive, striking that fine balance between efficiency and genuine hospitality. You won’t find the kind of aloof, theatrical service one might expect at a temple of haute cuisine, but rather a team that seems genuinely pleased to see you well-fed and content.

All in all, Jin Zhu is a solid choice if you want a well-paced, well-portioned meal in good company.  Just don’t expect any of the dishes to haunt your dreams.

Highly recommended. Was looking for some Taiwanese dinner and this came up as an option with good rating. No doubt about it. We took the set meal which has adequate options to choose from. The appetizer selected was the fried pork belly which was good. The mains were excellent i.e. the stinky tauhu fried with century eggs, beef slices fried with onion, oysters on fried yu tiaw and the stir fried cabbage with dried shrimps. The soup option was again something different i.e. chicken plus yam (different type of yam and not the one which we are used to). Tasted excellent. There was a mix up of the soup option. As a result, a waiter came over to offer us some side cold dishes. He recommended the salted fried peanuts, sweet & sour baby tomatos and garlic cucumber. All were really good. As some one who is a fan of DTF, this place beats them hands down.

A special call out to the service that was rendered. It is no less than excellent. From the start when we arrived at the restaurant (with no reservation), till the end of our meal. Kudos to the service team. The dining area was also really comfortable.
My first meal in Taipei. I am not sure if they are authentic Taiwanese dishes. I like their services, and environment. Food are pretty decent, recommended to try 真珠小炒！

More like 4.5 ⭐ Knowing absolutely nothing about this place, relied totally on Google community, and they didn't let us down, what a great Taiwanese restaurant.

FOOD: really very nice, great range of menu, but do becareful of the Stinky Tofu a really an acquired taste, haa haa haa. 9/10.

SERVICE: good standard for this tier, can't complain. 8/10.

FACILITY: since it sits in a shopping mall, facilities are good. The restaurant itself has great house keeping, spacious (not too any tables) and relevant design. 8/10.

PRICE: very acceptable 😂 8/10.

It’s been a long time haven’t been back to Taipei.

I’m impressed for the exception service that the host at the reception - Mr Wang let us having the best dining experience on the 10th November (late lunch time).

We didn’t make any reservation so only can queue for the seats, and the desert not even late-served as he mentioned, but he offered us as complimentary to make this hospitality level more stunning.

Will definitely recommend for friends and family to visit.

reviews.text: Hands down one of the top five Italian restaurants in Taipei. All the servers are very knowledgeable of Italian food. The place is nicely decorated and makes you feel warm and cozy.
I am very impressed by the food, esp the rigatoni with sausage meat and mushroom which has such rich flavour and the pasta is cooked to perfection.

A local Italian YT recommended this authentic Italian restaurant. The waiters are knowledgeable of the daily specials and the menu. The Italian wine recommended was adequate for what we wanted.  Attentive and quick service.  The dishes are flavourful and small on the portion as this is not a family style Italian restaurant.  Risotto was full of flavour and gnocchi was heavenly light with a heavy white sauce.  Desserts are tasty and proper.

This is the absolute hidden gem of Taipei. I love Italian food so I always want to explore what it's like in every country I visit. This one is by far the best one I know now. Apart from great food and drinks, the service is also great. Every staff member is helpful and kind and the menu and day specials are all fantastic. It is nicely decorated and for me the location was also convenient. I can really recommend this place, I love it and I will be back soon. Ciao!

La Mole came highly recommended by an Italian coworker, and it certainly lived up to the hype. The pasta was outstanding, cooked to perfection and bursting with flavor. Beyond the delicious food, the service was exceptional, with attentive staff ensuring a memorable dining experience. If you're in Taipei and craving authentic Italian cuisine, La Mole is a must-visit spot that won't disappoint.

reviews.text:
Delicious taste and generous portions!
We had:
Salted egg tofu
Typhoon shelter soft shell crab (we highly recommended this dish)
Salt Pepper rice cake wth red eel
Stir fried seasonal vegetables
It was a lot for the two of us, so we asked to pack home the leftovers.
Everything was of Michelin Guide quality.

Made reservation and did not regret! I think this is Taiwanese cuisine at its best! Every dish was delicious and the ingredients were very fresh and handled well. Portions are big here, good for family and friends sharing. Restaurant is not very big and always crowded. The owner was very friendly and thoughtful when recommending dishes to us. The servers are friendly too. Definitely will come again!

This is definitely one of the best Taiwanese cuisine in Taipei, I highly recommended to try the best selling dishes.
The staffs are very warm and welcoming and the service is delicate.
Also read about the story of the chef, he has a great ambition to improve and upgrade the catering industry, which is very attempting.

The food was good. The Sakura shrimp taro crispy was our least favorite but everything else was good.

The beef, rice and tofu came out within 5-10 minutes, then… 1 hour later the Sakura shrimp crispy which is the appetizer and the soup comes out. But we already finished everything else a while ago 😂

But overall good. They only have 1 chef so it’s ok. Time for ice cream.

Absolutely amazing food, we ordered ahead and was not disappointed. Perfect place for celebration and a group of friends to gather. The only minor downside is that their biggest table can only accommodate 10 people.

reviews.text:
I recently dined at YEN Taipei and overall, it was a memorable experience. The ambiance and attention to detail were impeccable, and the flavors in the tasting menu were exquisite. However, for a price point of US$500, I expected the service to match the caliber of the cuisine.

We selected one of the three tasting menus, and while the dishes were beautifully presented, I was disappointed that no explanations accompanied them. It would have elevated the experience to be told about each dish, its ingredients, and any specific instructions for enjoying it to its fullest. Simply placing the plates in front of us without context felt impersonal for a fine dining experience of this level.

Additionally, I noticed a lack of attention to etiquette. There’s a timeless expression, “Ladies First,” but my male companion was consistently served first throughout the evening. This struck me as unusual for a restaurant of this caliber and left a somewhat awkward impression.

That said, the food itself was a work of art, and the restaurant clearly has tremendous potential. A few refinements to the service could make it a truly world-class dining destination.

My family chose W Taipei’s YEN restaurant for my sister’s engagement ceremony, and it was a fantastic experience. We are grateful to the staff for their considerate assistance with the traditional Chinese process. The food quality was excellent, with perfectly balanced flavors that made every bite a pleasure. Special thanks to Chef Stone and the Hong Kong Chef for their warm greetings and exceptional cooking skills. All the guests were satisfied with our choice. I highly recommend YEN to my friends. The entire staff and chefs deserve high praise.

Had our New Year’s Eve dinner here. The friendly staff and the wonderful view of the city was quite a cinematic experience. As for the food, generally speaking, it was excellent but some dishes could be better. My favorites were the crab soup, sautéed wagyu with okra, and the mushroom-shaped custard bun. All a 10/10. My mom’s personal fav was the steamed lobster w/ Huadiao wine. The meh dishes were the fried rice and the mango sago. The former needed more salt and the latter more cream and/or sugar. Overall, though, a memorable experience. Thank you for the great New Year’s Eve experience.

We had the roast duck, and some desserts. The roast duck skin was nice but the meat was a little tough. We also find the taichi sesame / almond desert a little too coarse for our liking. Service was ok but as the place was understaffed, the staff looks frazzled. For the price, the food could be better.

Enjoyed a great dinner at YEN Taipei while holidaying in Taiwan. The night view from here is splendid.

Top service - I indicated that I preferred a window table on my reservation and they arranged for it. They also arranged for a 寿桃 as I said it was a birthday dinner.

Food - do call ahead to reserve the Peking duck. I chose to cook the leftover duck in congee and that was tasty as well.

ps: I enjoyed a 10% discount with Marriott Bonvoy membership.

reviews.text: A Michelin 1-star restaurant inside the Madarin Oriental hotel serving delicious Chinese/Cantonese dishes. I typically do not like chicken, but the chicken served was so tender that it does not taste like chicken. The fried rice was also a must try. Overall, it was a wonderful dining experience.

Dining at Ya Ge in the Mandarin Oriental Taipei was an exceptional experience!

This Michelin-starred restaurant delivers elevated Cantonese cuisine that truly impressed me—every dish was beautifully crafted and full of flavor.

The ambiance is elegant and refined, perfectly matching the exquisite food. The service was top-notch, attentive, and made the whole meal feel special.

Ya Ge provided exactly the kind of elevated dining experience I was looking for, and it’s definitely a must-visit if you’re in Taipei!

As hotel guests of Mandarin Oriental, we realize this Cantonese restaurant has Michelin 1 star rating and wanted to try. Given the short notice the Hotel Concierge put us on the wait list on tonight’s dinner. We are fortunate to get in with a last minute cancellation. I grew up in Hong Kong and was excited to relive my fond memories of delicious Cantonese food.

My review is based on the restaurant has a Michelin 1-star rating.

We ordered BBQ platter of 3 kinds of - honey BBQ pork, jelly fish and roasted goose. They taste normal and I’m a little bit disappointed on the BBQ pork as they are very lean and not juicy as I could get home in Vancouver. Within minutes they serve the vinegar ribs and soy sauce pan seared fish. Cantonese like to enjoy food while they are still hot so I feel rushed (even they did not rush us) to eat quickly or the dishes would get cold. The garlic fried asparagus however, arrived quite a bit later.

As hotel guests they offered the complimentary taro mochi and chocolate square. The taro mochi are definitely better one.

We then ordered the mango pomelo sago cream and almond cream with egg white. Unfortunately they were busy serving other guests and the desserts were waiting to be served for a good few minutes and when I tasted the almond cream, it’s lukewarm that I needed to send it back.

Overall, good service - they changed our eating plates 5 times during the entire dinner.

Areas for improvement:
1. Use a smaller teapot if the tea is for one guest so the tea would not get cold if the guest cannot finish the big teapot fast enough. Or use a tea light burner to keep the tea hot.
2. Check with guests if they want to serve the appetizer / BBQ platter first before serving other main course dishes. Allow guests to have time enjoying the appetizer/ BBQ platter.
3. Hot dishes need to serve hot and not lukewarm.
4. For guests who are not mandarin speaking, if possible, have a member who’s more fluent in English to serve and communicate during the course of dinner.

I’m not sure the local tipping customs. When inquiring with the server it is still not clear if or how much we should tip - the bill has a line for tip. Based on my limited knowledge, in addition to the included service charge at 10%, I gave an additional 11% tip and hope it is sufficient.

Thank you for the hospitality.

Been coming here for years for reliable and delicious dim sum. Service used to be impeccable and the atmosphere nice and relaxed. However this last visit has left me feeling that the restaurant has gone downhill. Witnessed a main server cough behind the main service desk in the middle of the restaurant directly into his hands then proceed to grab plates and dishes to serve tables. Would think in a post-Covid world that one would either cough into a napkin or at least wash your hands. The restaurant was also packed with people and it felt rowdy instead of the usual calmer atmosphere. Hope the restaurant can improve on their hygienic practices.

I was interested in the restaurant because it said it had been awarded a Michelin star.
Everything was delicious and well-prepared.
Thank you for a wonderful time.

reviews.text: Shin Yeh Signature is located on the first floor of Taipei Marriott Hotel's Midtown Plaza and is an upscale Taiwanese restaurant that has earned one Michelin star for three consecutive years. The spacious 4.4-meter-high ceiling space can accommodate 178 diners, with modern stylish décor and refined lighting creating a comfortable and relaxed dining atmosphere. The restaurant offers over 100 traditional Taiwanese banquet dishes, with signature dishes like the Five Blessings Platter, braised pork, and preserved radish omelet all demonstrating exceptional culinary expertise. Although prices are on the higher end and reservations can be difficult to secure, whether for business gatherings or family occasions, the refined cuisine and professional service here make it well worth a special visit.

Flavorful renditions of local Taiwanese dishes served at a breakneck pace in a warm, modern setting.  The high end, dare I say elegant, interpretations of classic street food like 刈包 elevate home cooking to starred status.  It's understaffed though / you'll get your food fast but will have trouble getting drink refills, adding dishes or paying for your meal.

Had a simple lunch comprising of 4 dishes with porridge. The menu was very comprehensive but 2 of us in the group was not feeling too good.
Service was excellent and staff were attentive to detail. The dishes were deliciously local.

Modern Shih Yeh restaurant! Located in Marriott hotel! Nice place and always fully booked! Food are delicious and good value! Mixed of traditional Taiwan cuisine and new fusion dishes! Highly recommended

Had a lot of expectations of this place given the stellar reviews and the consecutive Michelin years awards. However, disappointingly, my husband and I agreed that it was good, not great. Not sure if it's because we didn't order the 'right' dishes, or they just didn't suit our tastebuds, but we honestly felt we still preferred night market style - eg. Pan fried radish cake instead of fancy xo style etc.

reviews.text: You can have a classic Peruvian gourmet and cocktail here such as ceviche and pisco sour. From starter to dessert were really good. I especially like the lamb. The service attendants are friendly. I had a great time with my date.

It’s a Christmas dinner for us and we really enjoy the vibes there. We ordered our dishes already but we see other tables ordered French fries, so we follow. I have to say, the sauce is so heavenly and it definitely add one highlight to our trip! The service is so homecoming, we’ll definitely come back again.

Excellent and unexpected.
Everything we had was worth having and more.
Good and efficient service, a lot of food options, nice fusion kitchen, good alcohol options as well. Phenomenal value for money even on Taipei standard.
High recommended!!

Absolutely phenomenal. While we were eating, we questioned how often you have a meal where every single thing is outstanding like this. We started off with the caciocavallo salad. The light dressing, cheese, and candied nuts worked so well together and were a refreshing start. We then had the octopus and mashed potato. Wow. This was my standout and I’m not even a big octopus guy. It was cooked to perfection and seasoning was spot on. For the main dishes, we had the chicken and ribs. Both were so, so good. The flavor is strong, but balanced, and the cook was expertly done. The chefs really know what they’re doing back there! We started out with two pisco sours during happy hour, then we also tried the floradora and earl grey buck. All drinks were tasty. It was my husband’s birthday, so we had the lava cake and ice cream as well. Very rich and indulgent. The staff was also incredible. Very kind and polite, and also worked with me on being sneaky to surprise my husband with the cake and a candle. We will DEFINITELY be back! I can’t wait!

One of our favorite go-to restaurants. They have an incredible variety of dishes from pastas, small bites, seafood, and steak. Highly recommend the grilled asparagus and chicken thigh skewers as a starter. For mains, their grilled top cap steak is one of the best in the city. Come hungry and ready to share.

The stir fried liver is interesting and quite tasty.  The young octopus does not clean too well and there are part of clear spine and intestine should be cleaned and removed. The 3-spice chicken is disappointing - cooked too long and the chicken is not tender. The radish omelette is the most successful dish.  Taiwanese sausage is sugar dominant. I guess if someone like sweetness in savoury dishes they would enjoy the dishes more.

Beat 欣葉 branch we ever visited.

Every dish was spot on, including sweet potato porridge.

Steamed minced pork with salted egg yolk was so umami, paired really well with porridge.

三杯雞 not overly salty, super addictive.

Cai Poh Omelette just perfect!

To-die-for pan fried liver, must try!

Highly recommended!

Delicious AF. A Taiwan staple. Some dishes are simple looking but so high quality. Steamed minced pork with salted egg yolk and the other vegetable dish I forget the name of. Also love the porridge with yam (or is that sweet potato?).

Make a reservation! Came for lunch at 11 am. Lucky they were able to barely accommodate me.
Our best meal in Taiwan, despite it being our first dinner, we never found anything better than this through our trip

A historic place.
A historic Taiwanese food place.
I go there from time to time, and it's always good food.
The place is classic with its old lived-in history, but always nice and fascinating to go there.

The food always good, and good, the only thing, I noticed a change in the desserts.
This time they seem less sweet than usual.
Too bad, but equally good

The staff always polite and caring

Recommended and recommended to try at least once

reviews.text: Fabulous ravioli! The Amarone wine was divine. The service here is attentive and professional. Highly recommended! The only downside is the dining environment: the chef’s table is too high whereas the bar stools aren’t quite high enough. Moreover, the restaurant space feels a bit cramped. In spite of this, I’d come back in a heartbeat.

The food taste is superb. The atmosphere is great, not crowded, amazing selection of Italy wines.

The service is great and friendly and able to speak English.

Definitely recommend it! Best in Taipei.

This is indeed a hidden gem in the city center. Authentic Italian food and the steak is really one of a kind. The taste of Chimichurri and the charcoal flames taste made the t-bone unforgettable. The vibe was perfect and the wine choice was versatile. The Barolo we had was a good choice that one bottle is yet to enough.

Service was very friendly, and the environment was comfortable and inviting. The tartare with the Chinese donut was a very fascinating combination of Taiwanese and European flavors. The dry aged steak was flavorful and especially tender! Every pasta dish was delicious and reflected the Asian and European fusion nature of the restaurant.

Had a great experience here: good food good mood and really friendly staff 🤍✨

Will definitely be back again!

Love their carbonara, risotto (pls try their tasting menu for all recommendations dishes .

reviews.text: The food was overall good and we enjoyed our time here. Perhaps the most disappointing dish was the rice, which was a bit one dimensional and dry. The scallops were just wrong - cold inside and warm-ish outside. Best part was the shrimp pancake although everything else was quite tasty. The restaurant was busy and despite we had a reservation we had to wait few minutes to be seated. The interior were cool and cozy and the service was attentive.

Top notch service! Our server was very friendly and very helpful when we were asking about cocktails (note they have a full, proper bar).

The fried rice was pretty good I wish it was a bit hotter. The steak was pretty much what I expected for this type of restaurant. Veggies and squid were excellent but the basil clams seemed like it was just a bowl of empty shells.

We really liked the vibe of this place, nice decor.

Food is 3/5 for the taste/price but service is solid 5/5. The staff were very friendly and incredibly responsive. But I felt the food quality dampened the experience, and I expected much more given the high prices.

We ordered:
1) 高丽菜 (stir fried lettuce): 2/5
Lacked fragrance or wok taste

2) 流沙包 (taro balls with creamy egg yolk filling): 5/5
The black shell looked intimidating but had a very crunchy texture. Inner filling was very tasty.

3) 猪排蛋炒饭 (egg fried rice with pork chop): 3/5
I would prefer Ding Tai Fung over this. The egg fried rice is marginally better here but the pork chop is very thick and chewy - I didnt enjoy the meat at all.

4) 鲈鱼 (seabass): 5/5
One of the more enjoyable dishes for sure. Sauce is very tasty with the fish.

5) 鸡汤 (chicken soup that came in a teapot): 2/5
One of the stronger chicken broths Ive had that came in a teapot. Tasted a little like 鸡精, which I can get at a much cheaper price. Not a fan.

6) Duck leg (鸭腿): 1/5
This is the worst roast duck Ive had. First time in my life that Ive seen roast duck being so disturbingly bloody. There was nothing tasty about this dish either.

7) Chocolate cake roll with assam filling: 5/5
The cream with notes of assam tea wowed me immensely. I greatly enjoyed the cream with the chocolate cake.

Mullet Roe Fried Rice with Sear Scallops ($560):
The scallops on the top were quite chewy and juicy. The rice was pinkish and had
incredible texture and outstanding taste along with the mullet roe. In my opinion, this was definitely the best fried rice I’d had of this year (2024).
Moreover, they did meet my demands for not putting vegetables like onions or cabbage.

Roselle and Lime Fizz ($180):
You need to stir first because most of them syrups are on the bottom.
After that, it tasted fairly sweet, sour and delightful. The great amount of the premium roselle syrups really made it stand out more.

In conclusion, the prices were unaffordable for most people but both the drink and the fried rice were definitely on the next level. The restaurant had a luxurious interior with a bar. The service was quite fast.
Overall, it’s definitely a 10 out of 10!
FYI, 10% service charge is included in your bill.

One of the nicer restaurant we went in Taipei. Heard that the fried rice was quite good so we decided to try.
Had the smoked duck fried rice, and soft shell crab, and other recommended dishes by the restaurant. It's better to reserve before coming as there can be a crowd during lunch time.
Overall, quite good! Do drop by if you're in the vicinity.

reviews.text: The waiting time was not short but the wait just added the excitement to the dim sum experience. All the dishes were very well executed and it has a wide variety of choices from classic dim sum items to a little bit more seasonal and adventurous. I especially loved the spicy noodle, fried rice with pork, aubergine, and starter kelp and noodle mixture. The soup dumpling was nice but my highlight was definitely the fried rice! It was so silky and delicious. The staff was very friendly and professional and it is worth the visit. It has wide vegetarian options.

We had an amazing lunch after waiting 1.5hrs for a seat, it was very worth it!! It’s a famous restaurant and even locals love them. Service was top notch. If you love dim sum this is definitely an upscale experience! The xiao long baos were served in a bamboo steamer basket! The shrimp fride rice was very filling and not salty!  We also loved the tea they served. Wishing they open more locations in North America since I’m not sure when i’ll be back in Taipei again. :(

I loved it here 😭 10/10 food and service. My favorite was their house special spicy shrimp and pork dumplings (?). Not only did the food taste great, but the staff were also so good that the whole thing seemed like art. Haha. Everything was so organized from the queueing to the serving of the meals and desserts. I would definitely go back!

Amazing visit and experience (again)! This is a goto Taiwanese meal option that is foolproof and bound to satisfy near every palate. They've got locations open internationally as well which speaks volumes, and the precision of their food and service is unmatched on the island and elsewhere!

You can eat authentic Taiwanese food here. The food quality is really good and fresh.  The food is really tasty and consistent each you go.there. The staff are very nice and provide high-quality service.
You need to be patient during rush hour, waiting time can be up to 1 hour. However, it's worth waiting.

Good was surprisingly good :) and yes normally I review at the end of the day, but they have a event with reviewers

Modern Toilet: A 5-Star Dining Adventure

Modern Toilet in Taipei is a one-of-a-kind experience that’s as fun as it is delicious. From toilet-shaped dishes to quirky decor, every detail embraces the hilarious theme.

I tried the hot pot, served in a ceramic toilet bowl, and it was both amusing and packed with flavor. The “poop-shaped” chocolate ice cream was not only Instagram-worthy but also a sweet treat to remember.

With great food, friendly staff, and endless photo opportunities, Modern Toilet is perfect for a fun outing with friends or family. It’s more than a meal—it’s a dining adventure!

Based on the range reviews that I saw of this place I thought that the food would be pretty bad but some dishes turned out to be surprisingly nice. Of course the main attracting factor is still the novelty of the toilet-themed dishes. Each person must order one set so that’s their way of making sure that you spend money at their establishment instead of having multiple people just share one set.

The curry pork katsu and cheese ham katsu was surprisingly decent however the triple sausage dish was not nice. You can top-up 60NT to have your drinks inside a urinal container which you can take home afterwards 😂 The milk tea was pretty nice.

Don’t expect too much and it’ll be ok. It’s pretty much a one-time visit place for me

The portion of the food is big and the taste wise is ok…but let’s face it, you’re here for the atmosphere and everything poop-ed or toilet theme!

As there was only 1 person doing the cashiering and waitressing, I can see why they made ordering via QR only.
We had a great time at this restaurant! Not only was it a fun place to take pictures, but the servers were very nice and food was good! Would recommend visiting :)

Reservation required. No obvious signboard so a bit difficult to locate the place. But it is just around the corner. I booked the wrong day but was able to be seated as it was weekday, so just waited for some time for them to prepare the table. I would say all dishes we ordered are spectacular, the pineapple chicken soup tasted unique.
This branch itself is not huge, and it can be noisy at times when there are bigger groups of customers. Service is good, they checked on us a few times. Personal favourite: bitter gourd with salted egg.

This restaurant lived up to its Michelin star rating as the food was top notch in flavor, variety and freshness. It does not have ornate presentation but has good size sharing portions. It was good to see a mix of locals and tourists which gave it a good vibe. Reservations are highly recommended as it is usually full and venue is on the small. They have  several liquor options to pair the meals with and the menu lists those recommendations next to each selection.

Lots of street food and we decided it was time to try a nicer restaurant for a change.

This restaurant is located 10 mins from Taipei Arena in a little quieter area. The restaurant is clean and we had a nice table at the corner.

The food was excellent. 口水雞is definitely my favourite. The waitress was very nice and helpful and gave us her recommendation since this was our first time there.

Overall a very pleasant experience. It’s a little pricey but the quality was there

Top notch fine Chinese cooking done in an unpretentious style. Dishes are uniquely Taiwanese including the 水莲vegetables, pork liver, oysters and tofu

Strong recommendations: the tofu and vegetables. If you have a big group, go to the soup.

Dongpo meat is very good, not too fatty and has sufficient bite but still tender.

Wine pairing is amazing value with unique wines and full glasses poured out.

We come here because it is a 1 Michelin star, we expect the food is not going to be cheap. however, for  a restaurant at that price range , they have a lot of improvement to be done. we book the table a long time ago , but we only seated just right outside the washroom, it isn't smelly or anything just it is odd that they would sit is there when there are other empty table available. They wouldn't understand simple English , and since there are no English menu , I need to translate everything to my partner and they wouldn't even stop to give me time to translate. Foods are tasty but nothing to bring home, they could easily charge 40% off the price and gave me 50% off the portion instead . the set up of the restaurant most likely for smaller group of customers but the dish size is for 6+ people, you couldn't enjoy much of variety. Also, their vegetarian dishes had meat or fish in it , you need to ask to remove them if you are vegetarian, so odd, we spend over TWD 6000 for 2 people, definitely won't go back if nothing changes

EGGPLANT Parm, I'm not typically a fan of eggplant, but this Eggplant Parmesan, made with round Japanese eggplant, was an exception.  The combination of the tender eggplant, flavorful marinara sauce, and melted mozzarella was excellent, and I would happily order it again

GRILLED SOURDOUGH TOAST
ROAST CHICKEN
SEARED LOCAL DUCK

Apple Tart (too sweet) S&S CHOCOLATE CAKE

Searched via Google Maps for restaurants near the Taipei 101 area, and saw this restaurant that had high overall rating.

Went at lunch on a weekday and the regular seats were filled (we didn’t make a reservation). So we had to sit at the counter chairs.

There is a minimum charge of 600NT per person, which I have to admit forces you to order a lot more than usual.

The food is ok - not great. The pizza was overcooked and dry. The pasta was good, but not spectacular. The warm octopus salad was ok. Everything felt average, and it’s expensive to eat here since the restaurant is located inside Taipei 101.

Service was great though.

Our bill was around 1,800NT for 2 persons.

Nothing amazing here. Good atmosphere though.

Note that it's quite popular, so if you have a large group, make sure to make reservations!

reviews.text:
This Persian restaurant buffet in Taipei is a hidden gem. For 700 TWD ($30 CAD) per person, the food is outstanding – the closest taste to authentic Iranian cuisine I’ve had in the past 9-10 years. From the perfectly seasoned kebabs to the fragrant saffron rice and rich stews, every bite was a nostalgic trip to Iran. The flavors were spot-on, and the quality was exceptional.

It’s amazing to see the restaurant packed with local Taipei residents, while we were the only Persian guests. A true testament to how well they’ve brought Persian cuisine to life here. 5/5 stars – delicious, authentic, and unforgettable!
Some dishes (lamb, eggplant, falafel, salmon, rice, desserts) are excellent, while the others are just ok, but overall the food and drinks are very good for the price.

Outstanding experience of first time eating Persian food in Taiwan.
Persian restaurants are relatively rare around Taiwan but much more common in Australia. This Persian restaurant is a buffet restaurant which is special.
I started to fall in love with Persian food when having a trip there.

In the beginning, I ate a plate of Beef and Lamb Koobideh Kebabs and saffron rice.
Saffron rice wasn’t the best but still very good.
The Koobideh here was as juicy and
tender as that I’d eaten in Australia.
Chicken Koobideh was also juicy and the chilli sauce made it even greater.
The chicken wing tasted nice and savoury.
The Lamb Roast was much more tender than it looked, which was amazingly delicious.
I also tried a small amount of Dill Shrimp Rice. The shrimps were good and the Dill rice tastes familiar somehow.

In terms of drinks, saffron juice tasted kinda sour, sweet and similar to Passion Fruit and I liked it.
Iranian Ice Black Tea was also great with liquid sugar added (liquid sugar was next to the Black Tea area).

When it comes to desserts, I took 2 of each chocolate and original Fereni, a cream caramel, Muscati and coconut.
All of these were great and Muscati tasted pretty sweet. The original Fereni was almost as fluidic as a drink, but the chocolate one was solid. In addition, they didn’t make Saffron ice cream today, but they got caramel ice cream instead and it was beyond my description. If you want a scoop of ice cream, you need to go to the bar and ask the staff.

In conclusion, the price for this meal was $599 + $599*10% = $659. It’s cheaper than the ones in Australia. On top of that, the Persian restaurants in Australia are non-buffet restaurants and still more expensive.

Overall, it’s a 9.5 out of 10!
Unfortunately, there was no Faloodeh (Persian Lime and Rose Water Granita With Rice Noodles), which was my favorite Persian dessert in Australia. If there were Faloodeh, it would be 10 out of 10. But still definitely worth it to eat here again in the near future. The service, food and the atmosphere are all exceptionally good.

Great middle east food in Taipei.
One price for all you can eat, delicious meaty food, salad, fruit, rice and chicken. Overall is great and value to money.
To me the spice is a bit too mild, but still worth the price and experience to go for.

The restaurant is famous with many people in queue, it's better to book the table in advance

The dining experience was great.
The buffet offers a wide variety of Iranian food, all of them are cooked and seasoned so well. We tried almost all dishes and none of them upset us.
The drink is also great, though some might find it too strong (for the yogurt the clerk lets you first try a little).
The price is also very reasonable compared to the food they offer.

reviews.text: Excellent is right, this place is absolutely delicious! Highly recommend the cumin lamb skewers and deep fried mozzarella dessert. Order the dessert when you order your meal, as it takes some time to prepare. Totally worth the wait!

Good traditional 陝西 food with lots of options. This place has been opened for a long time and moved to this location a few years ago. This place is good for family and portions are just the right size.

It’s a very good Chinese Shanxi Restaurant in Taipei. It modified the tastes from traditional salty and oily to lighter and healthy way without losing its originality. The combination of spinach and A-Vegetable is very tasty and healthy. The dumplings are also very delicious that the waiter always recommends to eat without spicy. However, if you like spicy, you may ask for chilly sauce. Different noodles taste differently. It’s a very good restaurant to have in Taipei.
Setting is very casual, and team is helpful and fast service. Dumplings and chicken spicy dish just so so . But the lamb hand cut noodles although doesn’t look great is truly a treat ! Memorable

Unique China shainxi food! Must try! Really good taste and special. Good for lunch and family gathering and it offer many payment method not just cash. Definitely come again to try more different kids of food here! There is commercial parking next to it or you can take blue line shandao temple station.

reviews.text: 1st visited here in 2019 (I saw the date from my previous 5 star rating 🤣). Everyone in a group of 6 were impressed then. In Taiwan for a solo trip now (2024) and this is on my list of must go places. Manage to drop by today and still impressed with everything. I made a booking for one and they prepared a nice cozy seat for me. Compare to other similar range restaurants I visited in Taiwan, this is super vale for $$ They're so good in everything I dun even understand how they did not get a perfect rating. But u should know this is really good at 4.7 for more than  9k reviews

Fantastic omakase and fantastic food. I discovered this place from a quick google search for nearby sushi and lucked out in finding this spot. I was able to get a table for 1 and enjoy a quiet dinner to myself. I was impressed with every course and loved it so much I took my friend back here when she arrived in town. You can’t beat the value here for what you get… especially if you are used to paying USD prices for average sushi. I paid around $33 USD for the middle tier omakase option. Highly highly recommend having dinner here one of your nights in Taipei

Awesome food. The set dinner is like a 8-course meal with immaculate setting, presentation and taste. The soup is superb, constantly being heated and you can pour it out into a small cup. The tomato, covered in yogurt with salmon sandwiched inside, blew my mind. Very thoughtful of the little eaters as well. The kids are served bread and dessert right at the beginning. Highly recommend.

Always a pleasant experience to dine at Ikki.
Yummy food and super excellent service.
You can never go wrong bringing important visitors to done there

Lovely and interesting experience all around. Service was especially splendid, the dining area comfortable and attractive. This was actually a different kind of dining experience for us - usually, it's sushi, sashimi and accompaniments.  We both ordered set meals - my husband had the duck, and I had the waygu beef. Without going into a lot of detail, they were both good choices. The only thing I didn't care for was the pineapple  and bitter gourd beverage. It was a very attractive meal overall.

reviews.text: Amazing spot, chill ambience,a bit pricey, and really flavorful food. Sausage and fungus were the highlight dish. Every order comes in smallish plates. Easy to order either a paper form in English and mandarin that you can pass to a server. Cash only!
Amazing food taste and frozen cold beers! The food prices are reasonable and the portions are big :)

Very nice atmosphere. The bartender is friendly. There’s various choice of drinks, from low alcohol to high alcohol percentage. Suitable for heavy drinker or casual drinker. Overall the drinks are smooth and just nice. The place is suitable to take pictures, vibes are relaxing. 小豪讚啦👍

It’s a nice place for a catch up talk in a weekend. The foods seem to be Taiwanese style for casual drinking. Their main dishes are noodle and meat snacks. The foods taste are above average and the price is very affordable. It’s also fun to have a seat near the bar section to see how foods and drinks are prepared. The servers and the chef are also very welcoming. We even got some free drinks (the purple ones and they are not in the menu).
Highly recommend the pineapple drink :). Would come back again if there is a chance.
Really great food and fun environment!

plus_code.compound_code: 2GPW+FF Taiwan, 台北市大安區德安里

reviews.text:
My friend and I were just passing by, looking for a place to sit down and have a casual drink. Ordered a couple of nibbles to go with it.

Momo, who was running the bar, was incredibly friendly and professional. I found it quite impressive when I heard she works shifts of ten or eleven hours, with just an hour off—almost enough to make you question your life choices. During our time there, she didn’t stop moving, but still managed to maintain that ‘I’m here to serve’ attitude without resorting to throwing glasses at anyone. Honestly, she’s the sort of rare gem you’d usually only find in the ‘fantasy’ section of the job market.

The little snacks were absolutely spot on. Next time, I’ll have to come back and actually try the proper meals instead of just using the place as a pit stop for my alcohol-fueled adventures.

There’s nothing more you can ask for, especially since Leblanc is like half the price of the other famous steakhouses in Taipei. Fantastic steak. This is a must-visit every time you’re in the city.

Tiramisu was incredible too, get that for dessert.
The soup was great. Bread oily. Steak mediocre (ordered medium). Broccoli ok. Desert forgettable. The ”good” house wine was good. Service was fine. Not going back.
It's been a while since we were here, so we decided to come and visit again. Always a great and consistent place for steak and burger! Brussel sprouts were also a great side to all the dishes.

Great vibe & services❣️

The steak can be better cooked (ordered medium but it was overcooked). On the other hand, the lobster was fresh & meat was easily taken off the shell.

Le Blanc Taipei.vicinity: No. 183, Section 1, Da'an Road, Da’an District

plus_code.compound_code: 3J34+49 Taiwan, 台北市南港區中南里

reviews.text: Exceptional food from Cantonese kitchen. The restaurant is located inside Courtyard by Marriott Hotel in Taipei. And as I was staying at the hotel, running late and was hungry I chose to eat there. The staff is profesionslly courteous, but the language barrier made ordering difficult. I was, however, worth both the effort and the price, wich is fairly high for Taipei. All the dishes were delicious and some also quaint and charming.
Went there with reservation with family. The crew was all professional. Prompt service . Overall, dishes were fancy , scrumptious and filling. Worth every penny.

Food is amazingly good and the staff are friendly. The duck, hotpot and yee mien are must try! However, do not accept the watermelon juice promotion. It tasted like several scoops of sugar have been added. All my kids refused to drink saying it tasted too sweet and weird.

It was almost too perfect a restaurant, but the watermelon juice fell short.

The roasted goose needs reservation in advance, 3 days earlier, but the tastes in all 4 dishes are all great, up to the expectations I had before my visit.
The service provided by various waiters and waitresses is great and consistent.
The fifth star would be there if the air conditioning was good enough. It was too hot during our meal period even when we asked for a lower temperature.

Located on level 8 of courtyard by Marriott hotel. Exceptional restaurant serving Cantonese styled cuisine, famous for their Peking style roast duck which requires reservations 3 days in advance before you can order the dish. The set menu I had was a complimentary dinner package with the hotel room and it was delicious. Every single dish was well made and delicately presented. Chinese fine dining. Highly recommended

Din Tai Fung Xinsheng Branch.name: Din Tai Fung Xinsheng Branch

plus_code.compound_code: 2GMJ+HV Taiwan, 台北市中正區三愛里

reviews.text:
Din Tai Fung has quality food, espeicially their soup dumplings/xiao long bao. I appreciate that they push the boundaries of XLB and also make sme dessert options like chocolate and red bean.

Honestly, I find that the food prices are rather expensive, and other than their chili wontons and their original soup dumplings, the rest of the food is rather bland and not as tasty as other restaurants. Their sweet rice wine soup was also lacking in size.

Got here at 11 AM ish and didn’t get seated until 1:40 PM — expect a long wait if you come during peak hours! We finished around 3:30 PM. That said, once we were seated, the service was fast and efficient. Dishes came out quickly, and everything was fresh and delicious. Staff were friendly and spoke good English, so it’s very foreigner-friendly. Definitely a must-try in Taipei, but plan ahead for the wait!

This is not the original branch, but near it. The original only does take out now. Nevertheless, the quality is very high here. We got in line at around 10/15am and there were 8 people in front of us by 10:30am, we were given a ticket with a QR code specific to our party of four. After scanning it, we could order from it. Super efficient system as we were able to have our food prepared when we walked in. The food was super clean tasting, the service was outstanding, and the vibes were nice. Tea is completely complimentary here and there is always someone available to fill yours up as soon as you finish yours. James and Melody were amazing. My party was served in such a timely manner. Needless to say, the dumplings (xiaolongbao) are a must. The chicken was my favorite one. The steamed wontons were also excellent. Fried rice with pork cutlet is nice. And the cucumbers were delicious. You’ve gotta try it out when you’re in Taipei.

V popular with many people waiting outside, yet in good order. High quality food as usual, will not be disappointed. Very caring and attentive service team. Ultra clean toilet to the level of feeling comfortable to sleep inside (if needed)

I needed to come here so I could say that I have done the compulsory visit, but overall it's true - definitely overhyped. I have arrived around 11 am, got a number which stated I should come back in 110-130 minutes. It was calculated quite well, because after I come back 130 minutes later there were still 20 minutes till I get in. The service was very attentive and kind, I ordered the dumplings certainly and the rice with pork. Both of them tasted good but not revolutionary, I can easily get it in many other smaller places in Taipei. Without the waiting time it's okay, but it doesn't worth the wait.

reviews.text:
Beautiful restaurant, the food was absolutely amazing! We had the sets, an appy, soup, main, dessert, plus a drink.

Had wayyyy too much food 😂 but everything was so good!

We wanted to go to this restaurant already but found out my cousin also works there so we HAD TO GO! And it was amazing!

The staff were all friendly, they had an English menu, the head chef would even check in on us to see if it was good, and of course my cousin too!

100% recommend. I would say this is much better than most steaks houses in Canada, really well done!

I also love that you can watch your food being cooked in the back 😁

There wasn't anything I didn't like, and I'm pretty picky! Their cheesecake was also to die for.

My boyfriend was also needing some western food as he is not used to so much taiwanese food and it finally calmed his stomach down!

We booked the dinner here at 6:30pm to celebrating friend’s 30 years wedding anniversary, one of friendly staff Bobby served us whole way long, he is the best, he is willing to do extra for his customer and we all so happy for what he offered, thank you bobby, all foods and drinks are awesome and enjoyable, we have a very good time tonight, definitely will come back again when we are in Taipei again

Came here for lunch during a weekday cause I was feeling some steak. The food was average. Steak was cooked to how I wanted it, but the side vegetables tasted a bit bland. The plating was also a bit weak. Plate felt empty. I probably wouldn’t come here for good steak, but the have other dishes I would try if I do come back. Overall food was average but vibe was not bad.
The price for lunch menu is an amazing good deal.👍I really enjoy the steak here. It is tender and juicy. The tip change is 10% not like in the U.S..

Lovely place. Was informed that it is a very popular restaurant. Ordered medium rare for the steak but perhaps of the thickness, it seem to have turned out a little undercooked. Escargot was fine and the mushroom soup is a winner! Softshell crab salad is a little not fresh and I didn’t like it. Is it worth a visit? Surely a yes. A repeat visit? Depends…

reviews.text:
We ordered 10 dishes, but they arrived one at a time, making it inconvenient for groups looking to share or anyone in a hurry. It took 1 hour and 30 minutes for all our orders to arrive, despite starting our meal at 6 PM when the restaurant wasn’t busy.

Service was also lacking—waiters weren’t attentive and didn’t seem to be looking around. We had to wait about 5 minutes just to get someone’s attention.

Portions were quite small and pricey—not ideal for those with big appetites.

Overall, wouldn’t recommend unless you’re prepared to spend a significant amount.

This was the first time I tried this restaurant with a party of 8, including 3 kids. They put us at a table that was in a corner, which made it difficult for us to move around once seated. When you have kids and you reserved a table a week in advance, being sat in the corner felt like an insult. Especially when we asked about areas that the kids could play.

Secondly - the pizza was not cooked long enough. It gets a 1 star. For a place that specializes in pizza and chicken wings, we all expected more from here.

The wings were good for sure, and i recommend the salty egg flavor. It’s not enough for me to want to come back though. For the price and the quality, there are several other options in the area.

Chill atmosphere and impressive decoration. Popular restaurant in Xinyi district so need to make a reservation in advance. Fried chicken wings were tasty. You also must to try their truffle fries! Pasta and risotto were decent. Friendly staffs and reasonable price. Good place for celebration and gathering with friends. They will offer strawberry drinks for your birthday.

Super kind staff! The Tiramisu was average but the drinks were great! They also offered sugar syrup in replacement of flavored syrups for coffee. Great cafe for some cute photos! Take the number 3 exit at the 101 station and walk down the stairs to find this cafe. Minimum spend is 300 nt per person.

Easily accessible as it is right next to the mrt exit. It is a spacious place and once you enter you feel like you’re no longer in busy Taipei! It gives off a beach vibe with a bit of a “jungle” element. Their music selection is also great!

Food: the place doesn’t really have a lot of variety, it’s mostly fried foods, pizza and pasta. We had the fried wings combo and it was so good definitely a 10/10! We also had the pizza which was good as well and the garlic fries which weren’t so great cause they were too oily. We also got free drinks with my friends as it was a birthday celebration!

\u6d77\u7058\u53e2\u6797 A Beach.vicinity: B1, No. 18, Section 5, Xinyi Road, Xinyi District

reviews.text: Highly recommended place to visit! They serve really high quality beef and personally cook it to perfection for you. I was offered a private room and the overall experience was pretty great! Quite pricey but still worth it!

This restaurant serves very high-quality wagyu. Although the owner is a Taiwanese, the food is authentically Japanese. I had lunch there. If you want to enjoy a lot of Wagyu, ask them for an all-you-can-eat option, which should cost around NT$4000. I did not know this option at the time of ordering. So I felt infinitely regretful.

The fried rice was particularly delicious. The rice itself was filled with the aroma of Wagyu and it was not sticky.

The main dish was obviously the Wagyu. Even if provided with various sauces, I think the Wagyu tastes best with sea salt.

The dessert came with a pleasant surprise. It was a homemade jello with a fresh grape inside.

The service was excellent. The waiters and waitresses were super friendly and talkative.

I visited mid-week around 7pm and was surprised to find that only one of the three set meals featured Matsusaka beef, despite the restaurant's name. Service from the front-of-house was lacking, but Eason's table-side service was exceptional.

Unfortunately, the quality of the meats left much to be desired. Despite the cuts being decent, the flavor and depth you'd expect from A5 Wagyu were absent, leaving me questioning whether I had lost my sense of taste to COVID.

At this price point, the lack of consistent service and subpar food quality in what should have been an intimate dining experience was disappointing. It's a shame, as the concept had potential, but it fell short on several key fronts.

Very nice service and environment leading to wonderful experiences to enjoy food and your companies before I visited many good yakiniku restaurants. They not only provide good charcoal grilling stoves for yakinuku, but they also provide hot pot for seafood for all possible customized menu if you have budget. Overall, I spend similar amount of money in many good restaurants, but I will come back again due to quality of food and service.

Food is good but they are understaffed; we walked in on our own with no one at the door
We waited quite a while before they came to take our order, and after the meat was brought out to our table, no staff had the time to grill for us until we reminded them again.
Atmosphere & table arrangement were weird coz we have to face the table of strangers sitting close n directly opp us to eat 😞

We ordered the set which has both grill n sukiyaki
The meat was very well seasoned , tender and juicy! There was a good mix of other food like fruit bowl, soup, rice served so it’s not too greasy.
Super filling and satisfied!
Overall I’d still go back again for the food !
