plus_code.compound_code: 4G4F+2Q Taiwan, 台北市士林區德行里

reviews.text: We arrived and checked in to get a numbered ticket. Waited for about 25 minutes for late lunch on a Friday.  After called back to the entrance, it had a robot leading us to our table. The decorations were modern, and the brand name was carved onto the seat back. We scanned the QR code to order dishes, and a staff came to confirm our order within a minute. The pork and the vegetables soup dumplings were juicy and delicious as usual. The steamed open dumplings were topped with shrimp. The appetizers were all great to be paired with dumplings. The hot and sour soup was well made, but smaller than what we expected. The pork chop fried rice with eggs fit in nicely to conclude our lunch.

It’s a very popular steamed dumpling and Xiao long bao place in the basement of SOGO. The average wait time to get in is 1 hour. Once you get in, the service is good and the dishes and dumplings are solid. What makes their dumplings special is that the outer skin is very thin so most of what enters your mouth is filling and flavour. Would recommend the truffle dumpling which is sold individually and the red bean filled dumplings for dessert. The drunken chicken was juicy and tender too. You need to order lots of dishes to get full as portions are on the smaller side.

Fast service, efficient, great staff, average food, and high prices.

The wait isn't too bad (45 minutes) and they have a website you can monitor to keep track of the queue. Since it's connected to the mall, there are plenty of ways to stay busy. The staff are all very friendly, the waitresses are cute, and the atmosphere is nice. Food comes out quickly at a good pace. Some of the items are really tasty but most are average. The price is high and I believe there are better options around. I understand why it's popular though, it's a very pleasant experience.

tasty food. this branch had the least lines i saw (out of xinsheng, fuxing, and taipei 101) but it could just be due to the time we went. we went as a group of 4 at 3pm on a tuesday and had to wait 20 min.

Everytime I dine at this place, or any of their locations, I am reminded how great the service is here. Taiwanese people know how to work efficiently and provide a dinning experience. When compared to the service from the American dinning industry, I have to sake my head. Thank you Din Tai Fung and crew, for always providing me with a great experience of service and fresh food prepared perfectly!

Din Tai Fung Tianmu Restaurant.vicinity: B1, No. 77號, 中山北路六段, Shilin District

plus_code.compound_code: 3G7J+52 Taiwan, 台北市中山區新福里

reviews.text: I had an amazing dinner with the La Legend meal set. There is no sommelier service but the wine pairings were delectable.starting with a rose champagne, chardonnay, and ending with a Pinot noir. Every wine were all on the sweet side and not dry.

Had a wonderful time here. Amazing atmosphere, service and food!!

This is the first time i brought my wife to explore Taiwan and we decide to eat at the beautiful restaurant. The servers were extremely patient explaining every dish to us in English as my wife does not understand Mandarin.

Every dish was spectacular and would highly recommend this place to anyone who would like to experience new things.

Outstanding cuisines with French-Japanese infusion♥️
Love the way of cooking for king pawn and beltfish dishes.
The service is very nice with warmness.
Had a great time in dining here :)

So much care was placed on the theatrics (a bottle of perfume with one dish, a wireless speaker with soundtrack on your table for another) that the actual service and food experience is second rate.  Service wise, it's obvious the restaurant didn't have enough props (the perfume, the speaker) because guests are not allowed to sit down until their reservation time - Ie if you show up 15 minutes early, prepare to stand outside the restaurant.  Also it takes almost an hour to get your first appetizer.  Food wise, some dishes were good (grilled iberico), but none particularly memorable (the usual fusion with Taiwanese ingredients).

Everything is presented perfectly and delicately. You can feel the creativity and passion for the food from the chef. Absolutely impressive..and the dining environment is very enjoyable and the staff is very friendly.

For the set dish I ordered is 4500 wagyu ntd without tax and the wine paring is five glasses around 2500 or 2800 ntd. For the wine paring I think it's a bit pricy and the serving size of the wine is a bit smaller than that in most other restaurants.

I went there in June 2022 before it got Michelin star and now the cost of the same menu seems 5800 ntd now.

reviews.text:
Nothing but 5-stars across the board. Came here with my gf to celebrate her birthday. We ordered the lobster & assorted seafood for 2 set menu, which includes your choice of 1 of 5 appetizers (I got the duck) and 1 of 5 desserts.

Everything was incredibly fresh and delicious- not too salty either! They cook the seafood for you which is a plus if you don’t want to get your paws dirty.

Hoping to bring my family here again.

Jacky served us wonderfully. So far this is the best service we had after 1 week in Taipei. Food is big portion. Would recommend if you have 4 person , order 3 sets & then add on ala carte later if need to top up.

The food was very fresh and the service was excellent, There was an issue with the payment, but they responded kindly and quickly, and we are currently waiting for the resolution. Overall, I think it is a decent restaurant
It is very good. Highly recommend!

Very famous shabu in Taipei. The soup is so nice. There type of sauces provided are tasty. The satay sauce is good. The lobster is very fresh just alive before serve😀. Sweet and tender. The A5 wagyu beef is also best quality with intense marbling. They do turn soup into porridge.

plus_code.compound_code: 2HM8+P9 Taiwan, 台北市信義區西村里

reviews.text: Food was really high quality. You can see how much detail they put into each dish. Location was excellent as you have a view of Taipei 101 as you eat. Music was a bit loud but you were still easily able to hold a conversation. Only downside to this restaurant is how hard it is to get a reservation. The price of a meal is also a bit high compared to the rest of Taipei.

Came on a Friday night and was able to get a table right away. Loved the decor and vibe. The kids meal was delicious and nutritious. My kids loved the unlimited bread basket too.

My husband loved the fried jalapeño burger and I enjoyed my truffle mushroom pasta.

Our server was so attentive and nice. She even noticed our older child wanted the coloring sheet that was only set out for our toddler and got her one too ❤️.

Highly recommend!

The food for me is not so tempting but healthy and nice. The drink is delicious . Compare to others American style restaurant in Taipei, their service was out of my expectations. Every staff was so helpful and friendly even I am foreigner. The big guy, standing at the door, supported me make the reservation quickly. His attitude was so nice even he can’t understand what I was talking about. I love the desserts, peach pie with cinnamon sauce was so good. Last but not least, the view of this one should be voted to be a significant view of the city. Highly recommend.
And thank you Andy, who served our drink today, supported to set up the curtain for us so that we can take a lot of awesome photos.
Nice experience in Taipei.

An amazing brunch restaurant on the 7th floor of Breeze Nanshan 🙂. The atmosphere and the service was a total 10/10. If you are able to snag a table next to a window, you’ll get an amazing view of Taipei 101. My family and I sat down without a reservation right when they opened at 11AM. Breeze Nanshan does not allow guests inside of the building until 11AM, so if you arrive a bit earlier you may have to stand outside of the mall until 11. To my knowledge, the 7th floor is easily accessible by elevator and not so accessible by escalator, so make your way into the mall and ask for directions / look for signage that indicate where the elevators are. I got a smoked salmon benedict! This brunch item comes with 2 drinks (one juice and one refillable coffee or tea). The amount of food served is perfect, but I’d have to say the taste is subpar. It’s not terrible by any means, it is tasty! I just had higher expectations for this establishment as their reservations were completely booked for the morning I went in. However, I did see lots of folks ordering their pastas and their other non-brunch items. I wish I was able to give those a try, as they might have been better than my meal. I felt like the smoked salmon had a very odd aftertaste to it, and the sauce they use on the salad is a type of balsamic that I am not the biggest fan of. The odd taste from the smoked salmon transferred over to the bread and the eggs, so I kind of got that weird taste all over my meal. I love smoked salmon, and I’m aware that at times it could have a super fish-y taste to it but this aftertaste was a bit weird and it honestly made it difficult for me to finish the meal. However, the fries were good and the toast was also very good, so overall a very great meal. If you’re looking for a place to eat and catch up with a friend, highly recommend this specific location as their view is unbeatable. I definitely would love to revisit this establishment and order some of their other dishes 🙂‍↕️.

Trendy and healthy brunch restaurant we had for dinner instead  with awesome view of Taipei 101 if you get the back tables.  Sous vide meats, French toasts and pastas are all pretty good. This is a popular chain restaurant so you can't go wrong with them, like better version of Denny's. Give them a try!

SECOND FLOOR CAFE Breeze Nanshan.vicinity: 7樓, No. 17號, Songzhi Road, Xinyi District

editorial_summary.overview: Upscale 46th-floor restaurant with mountain views specializing in classic Japanese dishes.

The Ukai Taipei.formatted_address: 110, Taiwan, Taipei City, Xinyi District, Songzhi Rd, 17號46樓
The Ukai Taipei.name: The Ukai Taipei

plus_code.compound_code: 2HM8+MR Taiwan, 台北市信義區西村里

reviews.text:
Come for the ambiance, not for the food.

The food was forgettable, except for the dish with the white truffle, and it's not because of the white truffle. I just don't remember the name of the vegetable. That dish was really unique and interesting.

The food preparation on the teppanyaki was lackluster. The chef barely spoke and few courses were actually prepared on the teppanyaki. The chef just quietly cooked in the background, which made me wonder what was even the point of having the food cooked in front of us.

The views and decor are impressive. I visited in the winter so it was already dark by the time I was seated, but I imagine the views would be 10x better in the summer around sunset.

Such a BEAUTIFUL Restaurant! I brought my family to UKAI Kappou (Japanese cuisine) to celebrate. Great food and friendly service!
Must consider one of the Taipei bucket list restaurants to visit!
My family and I truly enjoyed the whole experience!
Just AMAZING!

We went there for the lunch dinning experience and were absolutly amazed.  the atmosphere and the view which were both incredibly stunning. The quality of the food was something to behold everything was exquisite. But for me the highlight was the service. Our chef くばるしーさん who prepared each dish with incredible detail and skill did not only make sure that the food was mothwatering but also actively engaged in converaation with us and gave us a lot of details about each ingredient and dish which added an aditional layer to our enjoyment of the food.

The other staff also did an incredible job making sure that we were comfortable and explained every option available to us.
If ever you find yourself in taipei this is a must visit.

This Japanese culinary experience showcases exceptional culinary skills and the use of high-quality ingredients. Situated on the 46th floor in Taipei, the setting offers a fantastic view, yet it tends to be a bit too quiet, especially for smaller groups occupying a table for 14 with no view except of the chef. The Kappou style, where the chef cuts and cooks in front of you, is well-suited for dining, but opting for a larger group or a private room with teppanyaki might be a more preferable choice. While the food comes at a cost, it undeniably mirrors its quality. Diverging from the traditional Japanese chef style, this cuisine leans towards more cooked dishes than sushi and sashimi. The innovative cooking style is apparent, such as presenting crab on the shell to relish the umami extracted from the head, infused onto the crab meat. The dinner's highlight was the claypot eel rice topped with ikura. It was a delightful dining experience, but financial readiness is advised, as the alcohol selection, ranging from sake to wine, is not budget-friendly. Great and friendly service !
Excellent food & service. A bit more expensive than its worth but definitely a delightful meal if u don’t mind spending

The Ukai Taipei.vicinity: 46樓, No. 17號, Songzhi Road, Xinyi District

plus_code.compound_code: 2HP7+34 Taiwan, 台北市信義區西村里

reviews.text:
Fancy looking restaurant in Grand Hyatt Taipei hotel. Ambience is expected of Hyatt standard and service staff is fairly responsive.

Food took long to arrive although there were not many people. However the taste is good.  Vegetarian fried rice was surprisingly flavourful. Seafood soup was too starchy and tasted more like stew.

The Chinese name of this restaurant literally translated to "Pretty".  The place is really nice.  The service was ok.  I think they could use a few more service persons.  None of the Cantonese restaurant around the Sn Francisco Bay Area can compare to this place.  The food is exquisite but not good enough for me to give them a Five-stars.

For lunch, I went there just for lunch to try out their Dim Sum.
I have say the quality is good, but the taste doesn't do justice for the quality of the food.  Most items are on the sweet side.  I guess they tried to bring out the umami flavor of the dishes but failed.
They also need to train their staff better, because I asked him the difference between the two jellyfish. All they could tell me when it's regular jellyfish the other one is marinated in vinegar sauce.
But the truth is the jellyfish in vinegar sauce it should be called 海蜇頭。
Which is actually a more desirable jellyfish section. Hence the higher price.

I was so disappointed since I had a great dinner banquet about 5 months ago.  So I lower to 4 star.

For Dinner, This restaurant is known for their dim sum and roast goose.
The Roast Goose must pre-order, but can't be combined with dim sum.
The short rib and 蘿蔔絲餅 are must try. So are their dim sum.
Nice Chinese restaurant inside hotel. Nice ambience and service and decent food. Staff is very courteous.

This is a Hong Kong style restaurant in the Grand Hyatt Taipei.  The restaurant has one part dim sum and the other full dish meals.   Overall the food is tasty and authentic.  The atmosphere is good and we liked the decorations.  The only issue is the staff is a bit under trained, or they are very short staff.  We had to call and ask multiple times to get things done.

plus_code.compound_code: 2HP3+GJ Taiwan, 台北市大安區敦煌里

reviews.text: One of the best fine dining experience in Taiwan. Perfect blend of Taiwanese ingredients and South American cuisines. Joaquin and Di are both great host. Will definitely come back again.

I've dined at plenty of Michelin-starred restaurants around the world, but this one was a letdown.
The dishes were pretty underwhelming—nothing exciting, and the flavors didn’t really work together.

On top of that, they served ice-cold hand towels, which was a shock, especially in Taipei's chilly winter!
Definitely not what I’d expect from a restaurant of this level.
I won’t be coming back.

It was a great experience trying this young but hot restaurant
Knew chef for long since Mono Hong Kong, more than happy to see he has created his own project with lovely wife successfully
The menu has been designed in respectful way to Taiwan local ingredients yet still can tell the stories brought by chef from his hometown continent, like most of them and surprisingly impressive by the Medianoche
雲林烏骨雞
The young team is so focused and dedicated, with a cozy and easy atmosphere

Very professionally-run Latin/South-American inspired open kitchen.   Dishes are generally excellent (with layered tastes and amusing backstories) when the chef goes back to his roots, much less so when the dishes veer towards more typical Taiwanese fusion (especially seafood).    Large staff, very comfortable seating.

Yes, it is expensive, but the service is impeccable, very personal, and attentive, the food is prepared in front of you so you can see the care and detail that goes into it, and the food is a careful fusion of Argentinian and Taiwanese flavors and ingredients. For a celebrstion, there is not just a card but a personal message signed by all the staff. I've paid more for less. This was June's menu but it changes regularly.

reviews.text:
Order: 1 small portion of flour-rice noodle

💛 The noodles and broth tasted great. The texture reminds me of enoki mushrooms, a great snack/light meal. The pricing is reasonable for the portion.
💛 There’s extra seasoning available if you need to adjust to your flavor profile.
🤔 The line is long, but the service is super quick and efficient. Limited English menu available.
😵‍💫 Located inside Ningxia Night Market, so it’s SUPER crowded to navigate to.

Small size is 65 and large is 80 NT. I prepaid for 2 small bowls on Klook and the cashier scanned my QR at the till. Lines can be quite long but is very fast moving!

If you don’t like slimy texture this may not be for you! I enjoyed the pork intestine pieces inside and the noodles were very umami and silky. They come with cilantro so tell the cashier if you don’t want that. Self serve garlic, chili sauce and black vinegar station. A few benches but mostly standing!

Have been going to their stall for years. Must visit for any first-time visitors to Taipei. It’s the classic street-style oyster noodles.

The perfect hot noodle dish to warm the stomach (and soul) in Taipei’s cold weather. The broth has a very umami smell and taste due to the bonito flakes used.

Service is very fast and efficient - you better know what you want before you reach the counter! Then again, they only serve one main thing on their menu xD just let them know the size.

Customers can choose to customise their own bowls with garlic oil, chilli oil and/or vinegar.

I went at around 9am, crowded but queue moved fast. I ordered and got my bowl in

Must-try takeout noodles in Ximending.
Line is very long, but it shortens very fast and it will be your turn in no time.
Can’t say its a nice visual… It’s noodles, but feels more like porridge or slime lol

You get a choice of coriander topping which i recommend. There is also a condiment station with chili sauce, garlic sauce and black vinegar. I put all three in my food and it definitely elevated the flavor.

Food is not bad but nothing super special. They have a sauce bar on the side and it tasted a lot better after I put in some spicy sauce. You’ll see that there is a really long line but actually it goes down pretty quickly so don’t be scarred to get in line, it won’t be long before you get your food. The place is really popular as you can see a ton of people standing and sitting right around the area eating their noodles.

Saffron 46.formatted_address: 110, Taiwan, Taipei City, Xinyi District, Songzhi Rd, 17號46F

plus_code.compound_code: 2HM8+MQ Taiwan, 台北市信義區西村里

reviews.text: It got such nice reviews on Google so finally booked it. Environment is absolutely nice with an awesome view. Overall the food is ok but not that authentic, also all the spice and herbs they used didn’t make the dishes memorable. Probably because it caters to the light taste buds in Taiwan? But it’s a good experience.

Every time we come to this upscale indian dining restaurant it's an amazing evening. Really fantastic food, every dish was good and some were excellent. Fun and tasty cocktails, and a beautiful room with a view of Taipei 101. It's pricey, but it's also absolutely worth it. Reservations recommended.

Food is amazing. Loved all the dishes that were included in the set menu. Drinks are superb, as well. The only thing that was bad was the service. There was a guy named Thibault (wearing black suit), he has that very indifferent face every time he had to serve our table. Totally unfriendly and when he presented the bill, he didn’t even say anything at all, just hand me over the bill folder and the pen. We were watching him how he was serving other guests, but it was entirely different. So, all in all, I felt weirded out about that. We had a fantastic meal, because the food was delicious but with that kind of service attitude, 🙄🙄🙄. The lady who served all the dishes was good, a foreigner who was kind enough to introduce everything, with a bright smile.

During my two-week trip to Taipei, I found myself visiting Saffron 46 almost daily for lunch, and it quickly became a place I looked forward to. Nestled around Taipei 101, it’s a little gem serving up authentic Indian cuisine, and the experience was something I couldn’t get enough of.

The restaurant has a cozy and welcoming vibe, with a spacious interior and great views of the city. The service was excellent – the staff were always friendly and attentive, which made each visit feel relaxed and enjoyable.

Now, the food – that’s where the real highlight was. I couldn’t get enough of their mutton dishes, especially the Rogan Josh. The meat was so tender and flavorful, cooked just right with all those amazing spices. The jumbo prawns and bay prawn dishes were also excellent – fresh, perfectly cooked, and full of flavor. If you’re in the mood for variety, their thali set is perfect for lunch. It lets you try a little bit of everything, which was great when I was in the mood for a hearty meal.

For dessert, I had to try their gulab jamon with ice cream, and it didn’t disappoint. Sweet, warm, and the ice cream added a nice touch to balance the richness. It was a perfect end to my meals.

However, if you’re planning to try some of the smaller snacks, I’d say steer clear of the pani poori and aloo tiki chat – they weren’t as great as the main dishes. And for anyone who loves some heat, the mutton vindaloo definitely packs a punch with its spiciness.

One tip I’d give is to book a seat ahead of time, especially during rush hours. It can get pretty busy, and booking via Google or giving them a quick call ensures you don’t miss out.

All in all, Saffron 46 was a standout for me during my time in Taipei. The food was delicious, the service was great, and it was the perfect spot to enjoy a comforting meal after a busy day of exploring.

This place is a epic view very nice spot to take a date or catch up with old friends. the food is somewhat mildly spiced for indian food but also very friendly towards every ones appetite 😋  the drinks are great the staff are very friendly and on it, and if you only speak English then the staff are very attentive to it.

plus_code.compound_code: 3G5W+CG Taiwan, 台北市松山區民有里

reviews.text: Wow we came twice during our taipei visit. 4 course meal special under 900 nt. The food here is spectacular!! The dishes are a work of art.

Lulu is such a great little spot—cozy, relaxed, and just elegant enough. My wife and I love it, and we actually had our wedding reception dinner there, so it’s a bit special to us.

The food is always fresh and really well done. The soufflé is incredible—so light and airy—and the lemon tart I had for dessert was perfect: tangy, sweet, and beautifully plated.

The service is friendly without trying too hard, and the whole vibe is comfortable and welcoming. Lulu isn’t trying to be flashy, and that’s exactly what makes it so good. Definitely worth checking out!

The food was ok, however the lamb was supposed to be 70% but came out well done. What I don’t like is the fact that courses are coming at the same time. We got both deserts while my partner was still on her main course. The restaurant itself looks nice and the staff were friendly, though looked a little exhausted.

Want to eat some comfort food after experiencing an earthquake this morning. I google and find out there is a high rated Italian restaurant , so why not. I arrived around 1 pm and it was a full house. But the table turn over is quick , I have seated after a 10 minutes wait.
I ordered Fedelini pan-fried lamb chop and vegetables from the lunch menu, added NT 150 for a set. I chose salad, black tea and tiramisu. The waitress informed today’s dessert is crème brûlée and can’t be changed except paying for the different. I just wanted to have tiramisu and didn’t mind to pay extra.
The lamb chop tasted good in general but a piece had tendon and it’s kind of chewy . I observed many ordered steak with pasta , steak may be their house signature dish. Tiramisu was excellent and the presentation was appealing. I would highly recommended Tiramisu to anyone who love coffee tasted dessert.

This time lunch with friend. Advanced booking made and got a window seat. But Chinese New Year gathering increases lunch traffic and restaurant is too noisy to talk. Consistently good quality food and nice presentation. Big thumb up for its hotel quality bakery!

Lulu Restaurant.vicinity: No. 9, Lane 113, Section 3, Minsheng East Road, Songshan District

reviews.text: One of my favourite meals in Taipei! The chicken and waffles & jambalaya are really tasty. Particularly loved the fried chicken. Staff was really friendly and helpful as well

In terms of Fish & Chips, the battered fish wasn’t cut into chunks but easy to be cut off with a fork. The coating was crispy and the fish was soft and had an incredible smell while just served. The Tartar sauce here was also delicious and got a sufficient portion for the fish.
The potato wedges were crunchy and fairly delicious with the ketchup. In my opinion, they always got better texture than the normal chips.

Tiramisu was sweet, creamy and had a tendency of pudding texture which somehow was the reason why it might be the most delicious tiramisu ever.
The cookies underneath were also delicious and nicely baked.

Fruit Mojito (Mocktail) was quite with a sweet, sour, and tangy taste.
It also had amazing texture of fruits inside.

In conclusion, both interior and exterior decorations were colourful and elaborate.
There was even a sand play on the patio.
The foods here definitely had its superiority even though the price was moderately high.
Overall, it’s a 10 out of 10 for certain.

FYI, you place your order by scanning the QR code.

This was my first time checking out Nola's Kitchen, and the food did not disappoint. The fried chicken and waffles were a delight, and the gumbo was creamy and flavorful. I will come back and check out the rest of the menu.

As a native Louisianan, I was quite excited to find this place. I haven’t been home in a while and so it was nice to have Louisiana style food.

Overall the place is nice and the ambience was cool. A lot of the decoration made me think of home.

The food taste was similar to Louisiana food. It isn’t exactly the same but I can get the feeling.

It’s worth a try

Food is delicious. Portions are great, too. If I have birthday, they give u amazing chocolate brownie.

The only thing the young guy waiter should be trained better.

Nola Kitchen Taipei Linsen Store.vicinity: No. 2號, Linsen South Road, Zhongzheng District

reviews.text: This is my favorite spot to get beef noodles!  Been coming to this spot since I was a kid. Taste hasn't changed at all! The crepe is so good... I love to put the pineapple mayonnaise shrimp inside of the crepe! Not many people eat it like this but trust me... It's bomb AF!!! Must try this place, highly recommend.

I visited this Halal food place during my trip to Taipei. It seemed to be a popular place for locals as well as visitors.
We placed an order for the beef noodles. The noodles itself were perfect in texture and thick. The meat pieces were tender and tasty and the broth itself was great too. I added my own spice to my liking. We also had the beef strips along with the bread and salad. Slightly more chewy but delicious. Taste was good. You can also drink tea as much as you like and it does very well with the food.
Upon my arrival I was told to sit on a shared circle table by the lady at the door. I kindly asked if I could wait for another table to be free so the two of us could be sat together I proceeded to sit by the door in the waiting space. She rudely told me to get out and wait outside. Very unprovoked and unprofessional. I obliged and stepped outside. I then seen other local customers walk in and they were permitted to sit at other empty tables. Eventually I sat waiting inside refusing to be treated in this manner. Her attitude was unfortunately awful despite no provocation from my side. If the management could offer her some advice it would be appreciated. She was the tall one who also sits at the cashier and seats the guests at the tables. Some kindness and a smile could go a long way in life.
Despite this, the food is great and I'd visit again to eat here and hopefully be treated better.
Thank you

I don’t who is the Michelin guide that is recommending this place since many years now, but they definitely need to review their taste! Out of the tens of restaurants that I’ve tried in Taipei for traditional beef noodles, this one is the least good!

Halal Chinese Beef Noodles (Da'an) is a great place to get your fix of delicious, halal beef noodles in Taipei. The food is fresh, flavorful, and reasonably priced. The beef noodles are the star of the menu, with tender beef, flavorful broth, and perfectly cooked noodles. The rich, aromatic flavors are a testament to the care and tradition put into each bowl. The restaurant also offers a variety of other dishes, all of which maintain a high standard of taste and quality. The service is friendly, efficient and fast. They got The Bib Gourmand award for many years,  an award given by the MICHELIN Guide to restaurants that offer high-quality food at a reasonable price.

I tried the beef noodles at Halal Chinese Beef Noodles in Da’an, a Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant, and they did not disappoint. The noodles were perfectly cooked (though i didnt like the big noodles type that much), with a soft yet bouncy texture that made them enjoyable to eat. The broth was rich, aromatic, and packed with flavor, yet not overly greasy. The tender, braised beef pieces added a satisfying and hearty element to the dish.

This halal-certified spot is an excellent choice for Muslim travelers craving authentic Taiwanese beef noodles. The service was quick, which I appreciated, and the environment, while simple, felt authentic. Prices are slightly higher, but it’s reasonable given the quality and Michelin recognition.

plus_code.compound_code: 3H32+W7 Taiwan, 台北市松山區中華里

reviews.text: A cozy Michelin 1-star spot in Taipei, such a local gem! The restaurant is elegant but not stuffy, and the menu is carefully thought out, full of creative twists on classic flavors. My favorite dish was the wheel pie, a perfectly crisp pastry, golden and flaky, wrapped around a filling of rich foie gras with earthy truffle taste. It’s pure luxury, but it doesn’t feel heavy or over-the-top. The rest of the meal is also delicious. Highly recommend!

Visited on 30/6/24

Unique flavours with fresh produce, but not enough to leave a lasting impression. Reservations were snapped up really swiftly upon release and thus we settled for a high table in the corner which was not as comfortable. Wine pairing was generally coherent. Service staff were slightly ticklish with their English, so we switched back to speaking Mandarin as much as possible despite not understanding some of the difficult vocabulary used.

This is a Michelin restaurant with memory spot.  First of all, the Taiwanese creative tasted meals that flaunt the spirit of French cuisine have the originality of the chef character.  Therefore, the current price is still acceptable.  The dining environment is lively and popular.  In other words, won't hear soft music or sounds of food being prepared in the kitchen.  When the waiter serves dishes, the customers at the same table need to be considerate and give up some space.
5th OCT. is the new menu for fall starting.  From making a reservation to confirming a mealtime, every contact goes over the kitchen's food allergy alternatives.  The tableside service is a gentleman, and each meal carefully explains the ingredients and the rationale for the dish creation.  Normally, lunch time should be 12:00 ~ 14:30, but it was already close to 15:30 when the last dessert was served.  Very French.
Chef starts getting ideas from Taiwan's food elements and cuisine characteristics, and then formulate meals one after another.  Each of the chef's creative meals is beautiful and meaningful.  Taste depends on personal preference.

The food was really good and the fusion was impeccable, comparable or some may say it is even better than the food that we have tried and eaten from the best restaurants in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand. I must really commend the chef for the extremely good service, food and plating, and would 10/10 recommend this restaurant for anyone wanting to try an Taiwan + other Asian country fusion of food👍👍 The chef also went out of his way to come and chat with us as well as take a photo!!✅✅

It’s a high end Fine Dining restaurant without “Fine” food

Super sad and disappointed about the food and service

Around 1/4 the food is ok but still far less than the standard of fine dining
They don’t even know how to cook lamb so the meat is super power-like taste without decent flavor
Sauce is nice
Dessert is great
but most of the min courses sucked….
Even their best brand- wheel pie is not good anymore
The dough pie part is not crispy and milky enough
They just use truffle to fool you around

They said the rice is super fancy one but you tasted worse than the average rice

Wine pairing is the most horrible experience
Only one wine is acceptable and others are super bad taste, which messed up my tongue and mouth feeling over the courses ….

I ate before and come back to eat here now
I’m so sorry for those customers in Google review feeling the same thing - quality has dropped a lot lot lot than before

Food is almost  4000 NTD …you can have much better experience outside with this price !

reviews.text:
Many dishes to try, some better than others. Long lines for certain dishes. The grilled king crab disappeared quickly, as some people took half the tray without thinking of others.

It was nice to experience, but I wouldn’t come back. There are so many places in Taipei with better quality at a more reasonable price.

Overall, an okay experience.

Fantastic view and friendly service.

We ate so much here it’s actually crazy. Wagyu cubes were so good it melts in your mouth. King crab (warm) was so juice and tender. Everything was great. From their seafood to their desserts! Definitely something to try once in your life. Paid around $160 per person by booking on Klook. Just show them the QR code at the counter and you’re in. Great views too!

The food is acceptable for the price range. The view is great, and the tea bar and wine bar are excellent.
Food is placed in four or five different "islands" with various themes. However, long lines exist for "high-value" dishes like lobster, steaks, etc. In addition, some "stations" are so small that you will miss them easily.

We asked to switch to a bigger table but were told we couldn't. I asked different staff members, even the floor managers, but all I got was the nonsense of "your seats were pre-selected when you booked your dinner with us." I told two different floor managers that I booked via Klook and was never given the option to select seating. Both managers said the restaurant "selected" seating for each customer without asking, and I asked based on what criteria. They never answer my question.
I wasn't being unreasonable and didn't make a scene, but I still needed an explanation as to why many other two people were sitting at a big four- or six-person table, but I could only sit at a two-person table. The restaurant was not at 100% capacity, and I could see many open tables around me.

When we were about to finish our dinner, a waiter told me a bigger table was available for me and my wife. Since we were finished, I rejected the offer.

I couldn't help wondering if customers who booked via Klook got smaller tables instead.

When you complete the survey at the end of the meal... they actually read and addressed the issue while you are there... well for us anyways.   We thoroughly enjoyed this buffet at the Taipei 101 building.  The entrance is by the office entrance and not the observation deck elevator area.   The food was fresh and high quality.  The lines moved rather quickly at the food stations.  We got our fill of food...so good.  We had nothing really bad to say except we wished they would come by with water instead of us going to the drink station for beverages as we were trying to maximize our food intake. About 2 mins after we submitted the survey, a server came to ask us if they can provide us with water or anything else.   Wow right?

A-joy exceeded our expectations! Everything we tried was excellent! Grilled lobster, scallop, abalone, king crab legs, lamb chops, A5 wagyu, tomahawk steak...all delicious! The Chinese food was also exceptional, the xiaolongbao was the best! Peking duck too. All in all a superb experience. If I had to name one slight disappointment, their desserts looked great but didn't taste as good as they looked.

reviews.text: Best Turkish food I’ve had outside of Turkey. Owner and his wife are very pleasant. No detail is overlooked. They are deserving of a Michelin star. Definitely stop in for a fantastic meal.

Authentic Turkish cuisine is not easy to come by in Taiwan, so we were very happy to find this restaurant!

They have an extensive menu as well as quite a number of off-menu cold dishes that you can choose at the counter by the kitchen.

The lamb was especially delicious!

Highly recommend checking Izmir out if you’re a fan of Mediterranean food.
We went to Izmir for dinner with a group of friends.  I normally don’t like lamb much but theirs was delicious.

Food was good and very authentic, but a bit too expensive for value. We really enjoyed the tomato eggplant appetizer and chicken kebobs.

Definitely call to make a reservation in advance!

We travelled to Turkey in 2022 and loved the food. Since then, we have been looking for an authentic Turkish restaurant in Taipei, that stayed true to its local roots and did not alter flavours to cater to Taiwanese tastes.

Izmir touched our hearts completely. The food tastes excellent. The rice pudding made us shed a tear of joy.

My finest compliments to the chef.

reviews.text:
The restaurant is located on the 85th floor in 101, with a very impressive view of the city, I came back to revisit after it opened from the renovation. I had been here 3 times before the renovation, and I’m extremely disappointed with this current visit after the renovation.
First of all, the food is mediocre at best, most dishes were not good, balance of flavors was off, main dish was overcooked, the main dish was not salted enough. Worst of all, the service was bad. Most servers were like robots, they brought the plates to your table and that’s it. They don’t explain the dishes, and then they don’t clear the empty wine glasses (as we didn’t order wine) not the used tissues from the table when they clear the used plates. The guests from two tables next to us left the tables for longer than 20 mins before the waiters finally decided to clear the tables, though the restaurant was already half empty by then. Also, the main and the entree took 20 mins to arrive after we finished our dishes.

We really enjoyed the food and drinks here. The crab meat starter with the fresh bread, the soup was delicious, and our main courses (lobster and seafood linguine, and the squid ink risotto) were extremely flavorful. We also had to get multiple refills of the black tea and flat white because they were fantastic.

The views were amazing, and the service from Janice and Lulu made our entire experience very delightful. Would definitely look to come back whenever we are in Taipei again.

This place was amazing - on the 85th floor of Taipei 101. The service, food and atmosphere was excellent. I ordered the mushroom soup, duck foie gras & venison. All of it delicious. The venison was so juicy and soft. We went for lunch. The service was superb and our waitress was in top of everything. I was very impressed!!

I wouldn't spend this kind of money but mom wanted to come here.  Food is pretty good and you'll get an amazing view if you're lucky.  Staff is attentive and there's a live band.  I deduct one star because this place is way too expensive.  You will need to book ahead of time and pay 3000NT to reserve a table.  When you're done eating, they'll deduct 3000NT off the bill for final payment. Tell them you're celebrating an anniversary and a birthday.  You'll get something extra!

This restaurant has great services, the food I would say it’s just above average in regard of its price. The best part would be the view from the 85th floor if you could get a window seat and a clear sky. Reservation is opened 2 months prior to the booking date, and it is highly recommended to make reservation so you could have the better seats for the view.

Lastly, the toilet is amazing. Got to go check it out 😂

Good Taiwanese cuisine . Rice, vegetable , pork are very tasty. However the restaurant should be clean (wall near the table is dirty) and it is not acceptable to have waiters bringing food with these kind of stained clothes

This is the one of the best Chinese food I’ve had. We stumbled on the restaurant on accident but ended up thoroughly enjoying all of the food we ordered. Drinks were ok we had cocktails a big expensive for the size of them but there were still really good.

The burgers were soooo good

Came here as a group of 8, we were offered a private room. Ordered drinks, and only then the waiter told us we have to order an expensive bottle of alcohol for the whole group to be able to stay. We just left.

Highly recommended rooftop bar in Taipei! As someone who loves cocktails, I really enjoy the drink they served. George is their nice and friendly mixologist, I got to try his first ever cocktail recipe 😁 The view of Taipei 101 and Taipei city itself is an additional bonus to the experience. This view itself deserves 5 stars. Cocktail is decent. Food with Asian spin is very tasty. Out of this wild gorgeous views from every corner. The outdoor seating has minimum 6600 NT. High price is expected.

Breathtaking views! The afternoon tea is a great midday break. Although the portions were a bit small, the delicious cocktails made up for it. If you go around late afternoon, don’t forget to catch the sun set on the horizon.

reviews.text: Portions aren’t big but nothing is overly greasy or salty. Service was great- Hannah was very friendly. Everything we ordered was delicious…. However!! We found a cockroach climbing on the seat and another (perhaps the same one) crawling on the table as we were dining. Mad props to one of the waitresses for catching it with her bare hands. They offered a small dessert to compensate but it was still a nasty experience. Would’ve given this place 5 stars if it weren’t for the cockroach.

We made a reservation here to meet with a friend and I had no idea what to expect, but it was all delicious! We asked for recommendations for dishes that were savory and/or spicy rather than sweet, and they gave a lot of great recs.

Vegetables aren't on the menu but you can order them, and the garlic cabbage was so good! We got a stir-fried tofu (tasted like fish tofu) and mushroom dish that was very good.

We got a salted egg chicken dish that was unique and savory, with very tender chicken. The pickled cabbage and pork wasn't my favorite dish, but had a strong flavor contrast to the other dishes.

We tried two soups and they were both so different from each other and so good! The black garlic chicken, mushroom, and seafood soup had such a deep and unique flavor, and the spare rib soup was herbal and rejuvenating. These soups were delicious.

I also got the guava lemon drink which was refreshing. In total we got 3 entrees, 3 drinks, and 2 soups, which is just a few items away from being the set menu, which we debated on getting (for a few 100 NTD more, we could get desserts and another soup). But this was already more than enough food for three people, and we struggled to finish it all.

I'm really glad we tried this place -- a lot of unique flavors I've never had before, and some really well thought-out and well-crafted dishes. I would come back!

Hannah did a wonderful job guiding us through the ordering experience to find what dishes would be best for our group to order. Everything was unique and delicious.

Overall, it is a unique restaurant that has a cute, relaxing café feel with tasty dishes and excellent service. The salted egg sweet potato fries were very good! As was the stir fried spinach and black garlic chicken soup.

Really enjoyed the food here. Well- cooked to perfection. One could sense the attention to details of the food here. Really enjoyed all foods, particularly thin sliced Mei Cai Kou Rou 😍.
Thank you

We visited during a period where they were offering a set menu with choices, rather than the a la carte menu. The menu had a good range of options and what we ordered was very tasty.

The wait staff were polite, attentive, and patient when communicating us non-Mandarin speakers.

Overall, the food was delicious and the meal was priced at a very good price point for the quality.

Experience the fresh seafoods in town? Try to visit Putien Restaurants (Taiwan Blvd. Branch) in Taichung City. Service is good with delicious and quality food.

Our initial impression of the restaurant's vibes was okay as we entered, but we were left ignored in the front area for several minutes. At first, we assumed it might be due to a lack of staff. However, a waitress later passed by and treated us as if we were invisible. This gave me a hunch that the service here wouldn't be good. The description of the menu provided by the waitress was quick, impatient, and not easy to comprehend. This might be due to inadequate training or her personal demeanor.

To be honest, some of the dishes here are unique and worth trying. After all, that was the primary reason we came here in the first place (the second reason being its 4.3-star review). The soup was plain and rather ordinary, while the hot pot main course was okay with a tasty broth. The "paper-wrapped rice" main course seemed overcooked but was generously portioned. Surprisingly, both the cold and hot drinks were served before the meals without asking for our preferences, and the hot drink ended up getting cold. As for the cold drink, it had no flavor and tasted like it was made by mixing water and canned jam together. Furthermore, the waiter collected our plates without inquiring if we had finished eating.

Regarding the cleanliness of the dining area, the table was not fully cleaned and felt a bit oily. The total cost for two persons, including a 10% "service fee," was approximately 1,500. Given the quality of service and the overall dining experience, I'd prefer eating elsewhere. If you're considering coming here just to take photos, that might be okay, but for dining, you should think twice before making a reservation.

reviews.text:
The wait staff were very friendly, patient, and attentive. The dishes we ordered were tasty, but not amazing given the price.

I would still recommend this restaurant due to it's convenient location, service, and the gift and tea shop downstairs.

Beautiful setting, great ambience and food.

The restaurant offered a modern twist on local Taiwanese food. The architecture is truly amazing, making the dining experience that much more enjoyable. Gift shop below offered very interesting spin on Taiwanese treats which were great for gifts.

Will certainly return for the restaurant and give the ice cream shop a go.

Braised Pork Belly with Mantou, Seasonal Vegetables, Lu Rou Fan, Sweet Potato Rice & Sundae - About 1700++NTD

We came for the sundae but fell in love with the food. The braised pork belly was so flavourful. It was on point. Eat it with the mantou that comes with it - perfect combination. Like Gua Bao but elevated. They said the green one was made with cabbage (couldn't recall what the red one was, maybe sweet potato?) - couldn't taste it but the bun itself was soft and fluffy. Red and green for Christmas! As for the vegetable, the cabbage was sweet. Naturally sweet. And it was crunchy. Not too oily. Both rice was good. Nothing much to rave about. The sundae - ice cream was why we were here because we didn't want to queue downstairs and dare I say their fruit flavoured ones were amazing. You can skip the tea one (we didn't bother finishing it) because the fruit ones were so good. After tasting their pineapple cake, we also went down to buy some.

Definitely not a cheap option but I think it was worth it. You can either have plain water or choose a tea for 30NTD per person. The atmosphere was quiet and relaxing. Though you have to take note that if you make a reservation for 1PM and comes early, they will not serve you until your reservation timing. Not even a drink despite the restaurant being relatively empty. That was a lil' weird but I respect their business policy.

Oh, visit their washroom. Pretty cool design.

This taiwanese restaurant is on the second floor of the Miyahara pastry shop a couple of blocks from the Taichung Train station. The food is great and the ambience is phenomenal. The shop/restaurant is housed in an old colonial building that has been restored and renovated. Gorgeous space.

Everything we ordered was delicious. I have been here several times and never had a bad meal there. Be sure to get the ice cream sundae for dessert too. It's amazing.

Similar to the previous post in regards of the building - The building is converted from a former ophthalmologist clinic dating to 1927, hence its Chinese name. The building is operated by Dawncake (日出), a Taichung-based confectionery brand. The building sustained heavy damage in the 1999 Jiji earthquake and the 2008 Typhoon Kalmaegi, and after the typhoon, the building was in ruins and abandoned. In 2010, Dawncake purchased the ruins, and over the next two years, refurbished the building into a restaurant. The store opened to the public in 2012.⠀
⠀
Moon Pavilion actually located in 2nd floor of this Japanese-style four-story structural steel building. The entire decoration is definitely worth to go for a visit, and even have a meal in this Moon Pavilion. As recommended in Michelin Bib Gourmand, Moon Pavilion juxtaposes colourful velvet banquettes with original wrought iron and red bricks for an interesting clash between the industrial and the Victorian. The food pays tribute to the old-time Taiwanese palate, showing delicate balance and shrewd judgment. Pan-fried butterfish over rice noodles, and three-cup chicken are the must-tries. Save room for the famous ice cream with countless toppings (there’s always room in stomach for desserts!).⠀
⠀
The first on-the-house appetizer (開胃菜) is Dried Bamboo Shoots with Peanut. Crunchy, nice appertizer, while waiting for the real heroes to arrive.⠀
⠀
📝Ordered 「紹興酒紅燒肉百頁結」- Shaoxing Wine Braised Pork - Definitely the superstars of the superstars of the night. That thick braised pork, with bouncy and tender texture, dancing in the middle of the chopsticks, is inviting you to take a full bite on it. Perfectly cooked with full aroma of Shaoxing Wine, you can use the buns (even the buns cannot fit the entire braised pork, just imagine how thick and awesome the meat is) and eat it. Each cuts are no lesser than 3cm thick (not that I really measure it with rulers, haha) squared. The 百頁 tofu (actually… many didn’t know that it’s not really a tofu nor soy product haha, but let’s just call it that way) is having crunchy texture and soaked well with the sauce too.⠀
⠀
📝Ordered 「蚵仔烘蛋」- Oyster Baked Egg - Served in a fancy plate, the baked egg has pretty generous oyster in it. Wouldn’t say it’s a lot, nor little, just nice. Perfect dish to go along with the braised pork rice, or white rice. The portion is not too huge, I would say that it’s perfect for 2 person, especially when you’ve ordered quite a number of other dishes.⠀
⠀
📝Ordered 「蹄膀肉燥飯」- Braised Pork Rice - Awesome. Wanted to go for the signature mullet roe fried rice, but was thinking that it could be too much, while we would like to save our stomach to savor the other dishes. This braised pork rice is awesome, and each fine chopped fatty meats braised well with the sauce, soaking each of the rice. Goes perfect with all dishes.⠀
⠀
📝Ordered 「30年老菜圃膠原雞湯」- Chicken Soup - Rich solid texture, that’s what I would say. Filled with collagen and chicken, this soup is rich in flavor, and you can definitely taste the herbs used in the entire cooking process. Definitely one of the must-order when you’re here.⠀
⠀
📝Ordered 「糖醋魚」- Sweet and Sour Fish - A little bit too sour to my liking, but nevertheless, still a good call. The texture of the fish is good, bite off easily without any effort.⠀
⠀

reviews.text:
Having been to many Cantonese restaurants in various cities (outside of Taiwan), this one is good but not stellar, and I feel doesn't justify the very high price.

The Peking duck was good. The chef paid detailed attention when carving it up, and even carved away the thin layer of fat underneath the skin. I have not seen that done in other restaurants. So that's a plus.

Vegetables, as you can see, is just... A plate of vegetables. No plating or presentation here. The jellyfish cold starter dish we ordered was the same. Looked like it came off a buffet table. Diced beef dish was good. Very tender.

Service was attentive. But we were given the bill without having asked for it, which seemed brash. When we inquired, we were also told there is no dessert on the house, not even a red bean soup, which is common in even mid range Cantonese restaurants.

The restaurant and atmosphere itself was nice. This restaurant seems to cater to wedding banquets, company dinners, and otherwise big spenders who prefer a nice atmosphere, but not to those who truly care about having the best food.

Live up to its reputation as Michelin standard restaurant. Dishes are carefully prepared to bring out its character. Distinctive big dining hall. But still not noisy. Good sound management. 👍👍 thumbs up

Service was subpar in my opinion when it says it is a  “頂級” （top） restaurant. We were just given the bill when we still had food on the table. We were NOT asked if we wanted dessert, NOT asked if we need to pack anything away. Lastly, we need to go to the reception area to pay for the bill if we need to pay by credit card.

Food was very average (it’s ok if you crave for Cantonese food but it is nowhere near a top notched quality restaurant). Roast duck was ok but the one we had at Yilan was better. It cost over $2300 TWD for the duck. This was just an average quality Peking duck that we could have at home but at a higher price. We ordered a jellyfish appetizer, veggie dish and diced beef dish. The presentation of two dishes (veggie and jellyfish) looked like food court style where they just scoop out the food and place on the dish (see pictures). I even took a screenshot of what they show on their menu for the jellyfish dish.

Also, we were charged for tea $60 NTD person which I never experienced at a Cantonese restaurant unless it was for lunch. Do not recommend this place.
Very nicely decorated restaurant with awesome service.  Very authentic cantonese style food

Been there a few times and the food presentation and the service is always perfect. However, it’s on a very pricy side.

Used to love their 稻草西施牛 with a hint of grassy taste. Yet this time it doesn’t seem to have incorporated the flavour enough …
Duck is amazing but single duck won’t get you many pieces. Unlike other places they will reserve the remaining meat and no 鴨鬆 to order.

reviews.text:
Taichung Rou Yuan is a must-visit for anyone looking to experience the rich flavors of traditional Taiwanese street food. This Michelin-recognized stall specializes in Rou Yuan (肉圓, Taiwanese meatball), glass noodle soup, and mochi meatballs, all of which showcase expert craftsmanship and deep-rooted culinary heritage.

The Rou Yuan is the star of the show—its translucent, chewy tapioca skin encases a flavorful pork filling, complemented by a well-balanced sweet-savory sauce. Each bite delivers a contrast of textures, from the tender meat to the slightly elastic wrapper.

The glass noodle soup is a comforting, light broth with silky noodles that pair well with the richness of the other dishes. It’s simple but well-executed, letting the quality of the ingredients shine.

Perhaps the most unique item is the mochi meatballs, which offer a delightful fusion of soft, glutinous texture with a savory umami punch. They’re slightly chewy on the outside but juicy inside, making them an unexpected but welcome twist on a classic meatball.

Had quite a fair bit of meatballs in Taichung but had to visit this because it is Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Visited the shop at 10am in the morning and they were busy preparing and setting up for business. Their official opening time is 1030am but told me to wait a short while. By 1015am they already asked me to get inside the shop and take a seat and someone came to take my order.
The menu is very simple,  only 3 items for selection. Of course coming here had to eat the meatball and also tried the fishball soup.
Food was served within 2 minutes and first look it was quite pleasing.
First had the meatball. The sauce covered almost the entire meatball you could only see a small bit of it. The sauce tasted very good and smooth and I liked it a lot. What looked strange to me was that the meatball was just filled with the chewy outer layer and there was only meat the size of a ball. It's not really like the typical where the meat filling is consistent across the whole meatball. It quite big, but on the tough side. Not sure if its because it needs to be cooked longer?
Then tasted the fishballs. Wow the fishballs were really good. Can taste the bouncy texture and it feels more closer to a meatball than a fishball. Soup is on the plain side though.
Cheap and rather delicious food. I would say the highlights were the sauce and the fishball. If you like gravy like me, go ask for more. The gravy in the container on the table is the same but it's the spicy version. It might look harmless but it's actually very spicy! It doesn't taste spicy when you put in the mouth but then the fiery kicks in in levels!
Worth a try but maybe go later when the meat are cooked longer.

No frills place, but the Taiwanese meat balls are amazing! My brother-in-law recommended this place because he grew up here and he is correct! I've tried this back at home in the US and I thought it was disgusting. But having it here was amazing! Would definitely return and recommend this place!

reviews.text:
Whenever I walk into a new restaurant, get greeted like an old friend by a charming crew, followed by one of the most amazing meals ever, then that day is a great day in my book. And today was one of those days as the Chef and his crew here at Tu Pang prepare and serve a truly fantastic meal.

The no-menu multi-course meal is envisioned and created and then executed by a fabulously talented and skilled Chef who takes top level (mostly Taiwanese) ingredients and magically turns them into artistic and scrumptious creations that leave you tasting and guessing and savouring every morsel of every plate.

As he and his staff bring each course to the table, one will receive a thorough explanation of the origin of the ingredients as well as the thought behind the dish which actually is a big part of the experience of eating here in itself.

I won't go into the individual dishes as they vary from day to day according to season and availability, but the duck breast alone was probably the most savory and exciting and yummy duck breast I've had in my life as it was aged and smoked and seared and plated to absolute perfection.

The restaurant is situated in a 60-year-old cosmetics factory that's been converted into workspaces and coffee shops and this wonderful place, and so the architecture and layout and decor add to this splendid experience. Make sure to make a reservation and enjoy a truly memorable meal at Tu Pang. 👏🫰👏

What a fantastic way to ring in the new year and celebrate our honeymoon. Chef and his staff provided incredible service that made our honeymoon celebration extra special. Chef's tasting menu was creative and delicious and was full of surprises. The wine pairings were perfect for each course. This restaurant deserves a Michelin Star! Keep up the good work team! Your creativity and delicious food is something special! Thank you

Thank you to The Kitchen. The entire experience from the presentation of the food and the thoughtfulness of the chef, allows one to fully understand the vision of the kitchen. The staff is lovely with very attentive hands. The ingredients very fresh and flavorful. At times one has to close their eyes to experience the flavors. Vegetarian and vegans are welcomed here as the chef can play with his creative mind and serve whatever is needed.

The dishes are very delicate. Bloody delicious fish with cauliflower cream! Very crispy and juicy duck skin.

It's really worth giving this restaurant a try as the chef and staff pay great attention to the details of dishes, creativity, and dining experience.

We had lunch here and it was outstanding. 10/10. Every dish was unique, presented well and great tasting. The service was excellent, special shout out to Jackson and Yang for taking care of us. Even the chef who is a true artist came over and talked to us. Every part of our meal was incredible I highly recommend if you are in Taichung even for one day to go eat at Tu Pang.

reviews.text:
First, I must say, Fleua de Sel French restaurant ,truly lives up to its Michelin-starred reputation. Everything, from the service, the food, the cleanliness, and the meticulous attention to detail, was impressively refined!

Today, We chose two autumn tasting menus:

1.	Longan wood chargrilled pigeon / Persimmon / Salmis sauce
2.	Pan-fried Australian beef filet / Potato / Black peppercorns / Red wine sauce

The amuse-bouche was a delightful start, with each bite both visually appealing and flavorful. The mini apple, with its perfect balance of sweet and sour, was especially captivating and truly awakened our appetite!

My first recommendation would be the Crab Meat Salad: crab meat encased in a yuzu-flavored shell, topped with avocado ice cream. Tasting them together was extraordinary—the rich flavor of the crab, the citrusy yuzu, and the creamy avocado all harmonized in the mouth, creating a complex yet surprisingly cohesive flavor profile. This dish truly outshined the octopus!

Another standout was the Roast Duck Consommé with Asian Mixed Leaves. Made by slow-cooking an entire duck, the broth was rich and robust, with comforting warmth. This was served with a duck meat dumpling and was an option paired with beef tongue.
As for the first main course, Butterfish with Caviar (likely French) served with a lemon butter sauce, was exceptional. The acidic notes of the lemon combined with the creamy butter sauce enhanced the fresh, oceanic flavor of the fish and the caviar. It felt as if I had been transported back to the sea, with the silky smoothness of the sauce adding an almost airy, foam-like texture in the mouth. This was an outstanding dish!

The other main, Abalone , featured South African abalone, which takes 8-10 years to reach a size suitable for consumption, paired with a rich mushroom risotto. Although I’ve lived abroad for years, this dish brought me back to my roots with its nostalgic taste and texture reminiscent of the rice my grandmother used to make. This may sound understated, but this was undoubtedly my top dish of the evening. I felt a deep sense of warmth and appreciation, as if all the hardships I’ve faced were somehow acknowledged and comforted by this one dish. Perhaps it was a hint of sesame oil or the abalone liver crisps, but regardless, I’m deeply grateful to the chef for creating this soul-warming dish on the autumn menu. 🙏
Regarding the Australian premium filet, I suspect the steak was sous-vide before being seared. Having tried many fillets around the world, I’d like to offer a bit of feedback here. While the filet was cooked to perfection, my experience with the wine pairing was a bit mixed. I initially asked for the wine list, but perhaps because I appeared younger, they only mentioned two pairing options—one with three glasses and another with four, including dessert, with explanations of the respective prices.
I’d suggest the restaurant reconsider this approach, as wine preferences, especially for pairing with main courses, can be quite personal. The light French red wine served with the Australian filet, while fine, was not an ideal match, in my view. Given the quality of the meal, why not pair it with a bold red from South Australia? The depth and richness of a South Australian red would elevate the premium Australian filet to another level. I understand that restaurants often curate pairings with specific intentions, possibly even budget considerations, but a South Australian wine would better complement this exceptional filet, bringing out the chef’s skill even more profoundly. For a Michelin-starred establishment, guests are unlikely to forgo an ideal pairing due to minor cost differences, so I recommend exploring a slight adjustment to the main course wine .
I noticed that the entire menu incorporates green elements, reflecting the chef’s meticulous approach to flavor and presentation. I greatly admire the chef’s artistry and extend my gratitude to the entire team for their high level of service.
I’ll certainly return on my next vacation to Taiwan. 👍👍👍👍👍

I recently dined at Fleur de Sel while celebrating my friend's birthday, and it was an exceptional experience. The restaurant kindly prepared a birthday cake for my friend, which made the occasion even more special. The service was superb, with staff clearly explaining each dish to us, enhancing our dining experience.

As a vegetarian, I was delighted to find that they offered a vegetarian set menu, which is quite rare in fine dining. The dishes were thoughtfully prepared and absolutely delicious. Overall, the service was excellent and the attention to detail was impressive. Highly recommend Fleur de Sel for a memorable fine dining experience!

I had the pleasure of dining here and I must say, the experience was truly remarkable. From the impeccable service to the exquisite cuisine, everything was top-notch. The restaurant even has a special parking lot for its guests, which is a great convenience.

The French-inspired dishes were a work of art, and the chef's attention to detail and use of high-quality ingredients truly shone through in each dish. Every bite was an explosion of flavors, and the creativity behind each dish was truly impressive.

Not only were the dishes delicious, but the presentation was beautiful and elegant. It was like enjoying a piece of art with each course. Although the prices were on the higher side, the chef and servers were happy to share their techniques and stories behind each dish, making the experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, I highly recommend Fleur de Sel for anyone looking for a dining experience that is both luxurious and creative.

For me, the spring 2024 menu was better than the fall 2023 menu. If I remember correctly, it's lighter, more flavorful and more creative.  The service is nice but I feel the place has too many tables for the space. At full capacity it gets pretty noisy

“Highly recommended for that special occasion with your special someone. “

The services and the asking price definitely were worth the Michelin title. Taste is a subjective thing, but we did find those dish designs can be a bit repetitive (e.g use of the “sauce rings” on the plates). Although there were some (good) surprises along the way, I was expecting for more “fairy dust sprinkling” moments. Perhaps in their next season’s menu?

Overall an amazing experience from the food and services, also thanks Fleur de Sel for celebrating the special occasion with us.

Since the Cold War is still on with my wife ( hopefully it will end soon), I decided to look for a relaxing place to enjoy my afternoon with some dim sum.

Yum Cha (literally mean drink tea) is a Cantonese restaurant with a relaxing atmosphere which anyone can enjoy on their own or with that special someone.

The sitting area is in upstairs which filled with nice soothing jazz (good thing is not elevator music, which can drives you nuts if you know what I mean). The service is nice, they just let you do the order with an ordering form.

I ordered a stir fry instant noodles, which is a classic dish. It was really tasty especially with the hot sauce (which you can get from the counter). The serving is just enough for one person. Next is the 蝦餃. I don’t usually order 蝦餃， but I read that, if the 蝦餃 is good, then you have hit the jackpot.  I thought the 蝦餃 was okay, it lacked salt and the skin was too thick. I don’t know if that makes the the restaurant good B or bad, but I had better 蝦餃. The last order was 蘿蔔酥餅， it was good, but again it lacked flavor. For some reason the dim sum was really light on flavors.  But I guess it’s healthy.

Overall, I really enjoyed hanging out, drinking the ying-yong tea.  And the noodles were delicious.  I would definitely come back again hopefully with my wife when the Cold War is over 😭.

Cantonese classic tea restaurant, which is subdivision of a famous Hong Kong joint. All my orders tasted really great! They probably retuned a little to fit local taste bud, so not sure if Hongkongner would appreciate the food. XO fried noodle is awesome. Only the drink is a bit disappointed.

I love their cha siu bao. It’s crispy and sweet on the outside and savory and juicy on the inside. It’s super good! Their crispy pork is a little bit too oily and greasy for me, but I like the sauces that came with the pork. Overall a great restaurant but bit on the pricey side !

reviews.text: Visited with great expectations due to reviews.  However, just poor service turned this into worst dinner of our family trip. Just 3 of us, and waiter did not really explain menu was all large portions. I inquired about gua bao, which they are known for, and that I was concerned about portion size due to our party of 3. He said no problem, I can change the order to 3 (but price for each bun would be a bit more, fine) and if you can't finish, you can take home. Sounded great, extra points for accommodating our smaller party size, so I thought. What he didn't mention was that he could only changed order for buns to 3 (for about the same amount of money), and the humongous meat order for 8 buns would remain the same--would have been very helpful to be clear about this before we ordered. WTF are 3 obvious tourists going to do with all the leftovers?! Plus the huge portions of the other two dishes we ordered?! My mom, indignant, got up to complain, saying she would rather we get all 8 buns (given we weren't saving any money anyway). What an unnecessarily uncomfortable nightmare of a meal. Tried our best to not waste food. Were not offered anything to drink, and it seemed like cold water had to be purchased, so we just got up and picked out water bottle and juice from the fridge to help down our enormous meal. Just, the worst experience at the end of a long day. Food itself was not bad. Included dessert was good, but required extra effort to not waste. Cash only so that was a bit of a stressor also.

Had a business lunch . Everything was extra good . Authentic , comfortable surroundings, good service and great company !

2021 April, I have visited there again, and I think it is better than a few years ago. This time I was impressed with the total performance. Better but hopefully I will enjoy the next time. Looking forward.
Good experience eventhough not the best in Taichung.
Main is ok. The buffet is pretty nice, but they only have white wine no red, which didn't go with my main course. Beef soup is the best dish in my opinion.

Jin Yue Xuan.name: Jin Yue Xuan

plus_code.compound_code: 5J2W+67 Taiwan, 台中市南屯區惠中里

reviews.text: It’s a solid restaurant for Cantonese style food in Taiwan. Their Peking duck, lobster and vermicelli, and mango pomelo sago dessert was all delicious. The vegetables, soups, and sides were also all tasty. It’s not the absolute best Cantonese food in the world with some dishes being average in taste, but overall, the quality and flavour of the food was very good.

Well known Cantonese restaurant in Taichung.  Many good reviews for lunch dim sum.  However, quite busy at dinner also.  Lots of fresh seafood.  All the dishes we ordered were quite delicious, no disappointments,  above average.  Services, unfortunately,  was a bit slow and inattentive .  Hard to find a server.  They first told us that our vegetables dish  was unavailable because they ran out.  Then, later, they said it was available, so we said OK.  But, waited more than 20 minutes and had to ask them twice before finally getting it.  Not acceptable for such a high priced restaurant.  So, the 4 stars are purely for the taste of the food!

Everything was delicious, prepared in an absolutely professional manner, so my biggest issue wasn't really the food, but the way it was served and the overall attitude of the staff. We received our dishes in a weird order, like whatever was cooked first has been sent to us first.

The staff also didn't care much about acting a bit "elegantly" or in a way that can be expected from this grade of restaurant. Whenever we got a new dish, the other dishes already on the table were casually tossed out of the way, like we were being served pork blood soup at a roadside food stall run by a 87-years old agong. We didn't really felt like the staff is happy about us, I don't know, maybe it's part of the Cantonese dining experience. The friendliest people were at the cashier, cheers for their 人情味.

Unless they use imitation ingredients, shark fin dishes on the menu are also concerning. No restaurant should serve such things in 2022, no matter how "traditional" they are.

Service was professional. There are clumsy moments with handling dishes, but overall very professional with communication. The price is on the higher side with smaller than expected portions. Some people may only get one bite out of the dish. Food was tasty with good quality overall. Atmosphere was good with fine noise insulation.

at this price point, i’d expect more from the restaurant in regards to taste, service, and cleanliness…

we waited over 20 minutes for someone to take our order, in the end we had to remind someone to come

the plates were slightly dirty and there were bugs occasionally flying around our table

the server forgot the sauces for our bbq plate (which was 1.4k ntd by the way!) and we had to remind them

there were only two toilets in the restroom but one was broken and the restroom didn’t feel clean

and the taste overall was mediocre for the price. for half the price, i feel like i can eat something of similar quality.

i just felt really disappointed by this experience and it didn’t feel worth my money 😔

Jin Yue Xuan.vicinity: No. 213號, Section 2, Gongyi Road, Nantun District

reviews.text: It was my first time in Taichung's IKEA. The one that I noticed is everything in the well arrangement. So eyes-pleasant and comfortable. The food is not too pricey, as I remember the cheapest one is the strawberry jam and maple syrup on 9 nt. You should try the french fries and blueberry cheesecake. Their ice cream is also cheap, you can get it only for 10 nt and self-service. There was also some tester of cheese chips. Overall the food is delicious and the environment is good.
Your typical IKEA store. Restaurant prices are on par worldwide.
Food is okay, clean environment, cozy vibe, perfect for day-offs mornings.

This is pretty similar to the one in Manila, but with more food and drink options. The Swedish meatballs and Daim pie are exactly the same. You will have to segregate the waste that you generate, then put the tray with plates, glasses and utensils on a conveyer belt. I think that this is actually better than just depositing everything on a rack like we would do in Manila.
A huge IKEA store. Could spend hours there as it has so many things! The restaurant and dining area was nice and pleasant. Had the New Yorker steak, tried the Ham and smoke salmon salad. Not bad!

reviews.text: Got pig feet and femur, both delicious. Perfect about of salt and a hint of sweetness. The meat and collagen just melts in your mouth. The braised pork rice was good, veggies were seasoned well and the miso soup was decent. Definitely worth a visit, price was very fair.

I like their braised trotter & pork hock. The sauce used is not too sweet yet savoury enough. Meat so tender till falls off the bone. Their lu rou fan & rou zao mian xian also nice. First time in Taichung and glad I managed to eat here.
A popular pig trotter rice restaurant, meat cooked so well it falls of the bone. Staff was really friendly and helpful. All dishes we ordered were delicious and affordable. Highly recommend!
Speechless!!! the pig trotter was even better than those in HK!!!  So value for money with many friendly servers who look after you with great food and setting. A must eat in TAICHUNG👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼

You can enjoy a budget-friendly meal with wakame miso soup, which is a bit different from the Japanese version, rice, a soy sauce marinated egg, and two pieces of Taiwanese braised pig’s feet. As someone who has lived in Korea, I didn’t find the flavors too strong or unfamiliar.
